title: Freelance Senior Product Manager / Product Consultant (w/m/d) – Abrechnung & ERP | Remote
description:
Du möchtest ein klar definiertes Produktprojekt übernehmen, komplexe Fachprozesse strukturieren und Anforderungen in konkrete Produktlösungen für eine eigens entwickelte ERP-Software übersetzen? Dann suchen wir Dich für ein freiberufliches Projektmandat als: 

Freelance Product Manager (w/m/d) - Abrechnung & ERP - 3 bis 6 Monate

Die Arsipa Gruppe ist eine schnell wachsende Unternehmensgruppe im Bereich Health, Safety & Environment, unterstützt von Warburg Pincus. Mit über 1.000 Mitarbeitenden, 20+ Tochtergesellschaften und 48 Standorten in Deutschland und Österreich bauen wir im Rahmen einer klaren Buy-&-Build-Strategie eine skalierbare Plattform mit nachhaltiger Wertschöpfung. Unser Ziel: eine der führenden Anbieterinnen im deutschsprachigen Markt - unterstützt durch zentrale Funktionen wie Finance, HR, Marketing und IT am Standort Berlin. 

Das Projekt: 

Für die Weiterentwicklung unserer Softwarelösung ginisuite suchen wir freiberufliche Unterstützung für ein zeitlich befristetes Produktprojekt. Der Projektstart ist zum 01.10.2026 vorgesehen. Die geplante Projektlaufzeit beträgt zunächst drei bis sechs Monate . 

Die ginisuite ist unsere eigens entwickelte ERP-/PVS-Lösung für Arbeitsmedizin und Arbeitssicherheit. Im Fokus des Projekts steht die fachliche und produktseitige Weiterentwicklung ausgewählter Module in den Bereichen Vertragsmanagement, Abrechnung, Zeiterfassung und Buchhaltung . 

Zu den Projektinhalten gehören die Analyse bestehender Fachprozesse, die Entwicklung geeigneter Lösungskonzepte sowie die Übersetzung fachlicher Anforderungen in umsetzbare User Stories und Tickets. Darüber hinaus umfasst das Mandat die fachliche Begleitung ausgewählter Themen bis zur Qualitätssicherung, Veröffentlichung, Datenmigration und Einführung. 

Die Zusammenarbeit erfolgt grundsätzlich remote innerhalb Deutschlands auf freiberuflicher Basis mit eigenverantwortlicher Zeiteinteilung und klar vereinbarten Projektergebnissen. Bei Bedarf können einzelne projektbezogene Termine innerhalb Deutschlands erforderlich sein, voraussichtlich etwa einmal pro Monat und nach vorheriger Abstimmung. 

Dein Projektinhalte: 

Fachliche Konzeption und Produktentwicklung 

- Analyse bestehender Prozesse und Systemlandschaften in den Bereichen Vertragsmanagement, Abrechnung, Zeiterfassung und Buchhaltung

- Identifikation und Priorisierung fachlicher Optimierungspotenziale auf Grundlage der vereinbarten Projektziele

- Entwicklung geeigneter Lösungsansätze und konkreter Empfehlungen für die Weiterentwicklung ausgewählter ginisuite-Module

- Erstellung nachvollziehbarer Fachkonzepte, User Stories, Akzeptanzkriterien und Tickets als Grundlage für die technische Umsetzung

- Übersetzung komplexer fachlicher Anforderungen in klare und umsetzbare Produktentscheidungen

Umsetzungs- & Rolloutbegleitung 

- Fachliche Begleitung der im Projekt vereinbarten Entwicklungspakete 

- Vorbereitung und Durchführung fachlicher Qualitätssicherungen 

- Projektbezogene Unterstützung bei Release-Vorbereitungen, Datenmigrationen und Rollouts 

- Dokumentation der erarbeiteten Konzepte, Entscheidungen und Projektergebnisse 

- Strukturierte Übergabe der vereinbarten Ergebnisse an die zuständigen Ansprechpartner:innen bei Arsipa 

Projektbezogene Abstimmung 

- Selbstständige Planung und Umsetzung der eigenen Projektaktivitäten innerhalb des vereinbarten Zeitraums 

- Projektbezogene Abstimmung mit dem Lead Product Manager, dem CTO und weiteren relevanten Ansprechpartner:innen 

- Aufnahme fachlicher Anforderungen ausgewählter Tochtergesellschaften 

- Fachlicher Austausch mit dem Entwicklungsteam sowie internen und externen Projektbeteiligten, beispielsweise aus dem Data-Warehouse-Umfeld 

- Transparente Abstimmung zu Projektfortschritt, Ergebnissen, Abhängigkeiten und fachlichen Entscheidungsbedarfen 

- Einbringung eigener methodischer Ansätze und fachlicher Empfehlungen 

Dein Profil: 

- Fundierte Erfahrung als Product Manager:in, Product Owner:in, Product Consultant oder in einer vergleichbaren produktbezogenen Projektfunktion

- Nachweisbare Projekterfahrung in den Bereichen Rechnungswesen, ERP, Abrechnung oder vergleichbaren B2B-Softwarelösungen

- Erfahrung in der Analyse komplexer Fachprozesse und deren Übersetzung in konkrete Produktanforderungen

- Sicherer Umgang mit User Stories, Tickets, Akzeptanzkriterien und fachlichen Produktkonzepten

- Technisches Verständnis in den Bereichen Datenmigration, Datenanalyse und Softwareentwicklung

- Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse

- Selbstständige, strukturierte und ergebnisorientierte Arbeitsweise

Hilfreich für das Projekt sind außerdem: 

- Erfahrung in SaaS-, Plattform- oder ERP-nahen Projekten

- Kenntnisse cloudbasierter Plattformen, APIs, Integrationen oder verteilter Systeme

- Verständnis für Softwarearchitektur, Microservices oder containerbasierte Systemlandschaften

- Erfahrung im Umgang mit Legacy-Systemen und Migrationen zwischen Bestands- und Zielsystemen

- Projekterfahrung in Multi-Entity-, Private-Equity-, Buy-&-Build- oder vergleichbaren Wachstumsumfeldern

- Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Occupational Health & Safety, Arbeitsmedizin oder Arbeitssicherheit

- Interim-, Freelancer- oder Beratungserfahrung im Product-Management-Umfeld

Rahmenbedingungen des Projekts: 

- Freiberufliche Zusammenarbeit auf Projektbasis

- Projektstart zum 01.10.2026 

- Geplante Projektlaufzeit von zunächst drei bis sechs Monaten 

- Voraussichtlicher Projektumfang von ca. 30 bis 40 Stunden pro Woche 

- Remote innerhalb Deutschlands mit eigenverantwortlicher Zeiteinteilung

- Einzelne projektbezogene Termine innerhalb Deutschlands können bei Bedarf und nach vorheriger Abstimmung erforderlich sein

- Vergütung auf Basis eines individuell vereinbarten Stunden- oder Tagessatzes gegen Rechnungsstellung

- Zusammenarbeit auf Basis klar definierter Projektziele und Projektergebnisse, nicht im Rahmen einer Festanstellung

Was Dich bei diesem Projekt erwartet: 

- Klar definiertes Produktmandat: Ein zeitlich befristetes Projekt mit konkretem Fokus auf die Weiterentwicklung ausgewählter ERP- und Abrechnungsmodule

- Remote und flexible Umsetzung: Die Projektleistung kann grundsätzlich remote erbracht und zeitlich eigenverantwortlich organisiert werden

- Relevanter Gestaltungsspielraum: Du entwickelst eigene fachliche Lösungsansätze und bringst Deine Produkt- und Projekterfahrung gezielt ein

- Direkter Zugang zu relevanten Informationen: Für eine effiziente Projektumsetzung erhältst Du die erforderlichen Informationen zu Fachprozessen, Systemen und Projektzielen

- Anspruchsvolles Technologieumfeld: Das Projekt verbindet ERP, Abrechnung, Datenmigration, Softwareentwicklung und operative Fachprozesse

- Dynamisches Wachstumsumfeld: Die ginisuite ist Teil einer PE-backed Buy-&-Build-Plattform mit zahlreichen Gesellschaften und unterschiedlichen fachlichen Anforderungen

- Professionelle Projektzusammenarbeit: Dich erwarten klare Ansprechpartner:innen, strukturierte Abstimmungen und gemeinsam definierte Projektergebnisse

Unser Auswahlprozess: 

In einem fachlichen Austausch besprechen wir Deine relevante Projekterfahrung, Verfügbarkeit, mögliche Projektkapazität, Arbeitsweise und Honorarvorstellung. Außerdem erhältst Du weitere Informationen zum Projektkontext, zur ginisuite und zu den angestrebten Projektergebnissen. 

Bitte sende uns für die erste Einschätzung: 

- Dein aktuelles Freelancer-Profil 

- Deine Verfügbarkeit ab dem 01.10.2026 

- Deine mögliche Projektkapazität 

- Deinen gewünschten Stunden- oder Tagessatz 

- Relevante Referenzprojekte, insbesondere im ERP-, Abrechnungs- oder B2B-Softwareumfeld 

Für weitere Fragen stehen wir Dir gerne jederzeit zur Verfügung!

title: (Senior) Finance & Accounting Manager (f/m/d) – bunch capital
description:
We are recruiting for this position on behalf of our partner, bunch capital. 

bunch is building the backbone of private markets, enabling next-generation fund operations through one integrated system that combines secure data infrastructure, AI-powered workflows, and expert fund services.

If you value ownership, growth through real responsibility, and working with a thoughtful and ambitious team, this role might be for you.

bunch is looking for a (Senior) Finance & Accounting Manager to be the backbone of its day-to-day financial operations.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role at the intersection of accounting, billing, payroll, and process improvement . You will be responsible for key financial operations, including preparatory accounting (vorbereitende Buchhaltung), spend management, and client invoicing across all bunch entities.
We are looking for someone with a strong accounting foundation who has expanded – or would like to further expand – into broader finance topics and take on more responsibility across the finance function.

You will gain direct exposure to the full finance function of a fast-growing fintech, report directly to the Head of Finance , and have the opportunity to grow your role within the Finance Team over time. Candidates with appropriate senior-level experience may join at Senior Manager level.

From day one, you will play a critical role in strengthening and optimising bunch’s financial operations as the company grows and scales across markets.

What You’ll Do - Handle all our preparatory accounting (including assigning cost centers and cost units) on both the creditor and debtor side (Kreditoren- und Debitorenbuchhaltung) and be responsible for exports to our external accountants in all our jurisdictions
- Own our spend management processes, including weekly invoice review and approval, credit card and employee reimbursement management, and direct debit setup, and make sure we pay our bills on time
- Run quarterly and annual invoicing across all products and jurisdictions and take the lead on reducing manual effort by working with our analytics and other teams to improve and automate our invoicing setup. You'll also track client payments and flag overdue accounts
- Support our monthly close by coordinating with external accountants across all jurisdictions and entities, ensuring timely delivery of monthly and annual accounts and that our external partners always have what they need on time
- Support on our regular tax filings, such as for VAT, across our entities
- Conduct monthly payroll reviews and serve as the internal point of contact for payroll-related questions — including social security, health insurance, pension contributions, and employee benefits — as well as financial employee policies such as expense reimbursement
- Support equity financing rounds alongside Legal, Strategy, and FP&A — including due diligence and data room preparation. You'll also pick up one-off banking and insurance needs as they arise

What you bring - At least 2–4 years of experience in an in-house finance role, reputable consultancy, or completed training as a tax clerk (Steuerfachangestellte/r) or accountant (Bilanzbuchhalter/in). This role has flexibility in its seniority — for more senior candidates beyond 5-6 years experience, we can offer a “Senior Manager” role
- Mastery of the fundamentals of accounting and familiarity with common tax issues arising in a multi-jurisdictional company
- Hands-on experience with accounting, billing, and spend management tools (e.g. DATEV, Stripe, Moss, Spendesk) or similar systems
- Highly organised and reliable, with a track record of owning recurring processes independently
- Genuine interest in process optimisation and automation — you notice inefficiencies and want to fix them
- Strong attention to detail and quality orientation
- A proactive, solution-oriented mindset and comfort handling new responsibilities
- High level of ownership, reliability, and flexibility
- SaaS and/or fund industry experience is a plus
- Fluency in English (C1+ level), at least B1 in German
- Be excited about working in a fluid, innovative, fast-paced, and creative environment and about being a part of bunch's culture
- Diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged

What we offer - Competitive salary
- Customizable benefits package (wellbeing, sport, mobility, food, and more)
- 28 days of vacation, plus 2 company days and local public holidays
- Remote-flexible hybrid (3 days/week in office)
- Up to 4 remote calendar weeks a year
- Work with a diverse team of 120+ bunchies from 40+ countries, with leaders who are best-in-class in their domains

Hiring process - People Team Interview (30 min) – Meet us & ensure mutual fit
- Deep Dive Interview (45 min) – Collaboration, ownership, and culture
- Case Study (90 min) – Technical skillset evaluation with our hiring manager

title: Associate Product Owner
description:
TL;DR Full-time. Berlin-based. No remote option available for this role. You sit with the PM.

Join GlassDollar as an Associate Product Owner and own the space between a good idea and a shipped feature.
Someone has to decide what "done" means, write it down clearly enough that an engineer can start on Monday, and stay close enough to the build that the scope does not quietly grow on the way. That is the job. You own it end to end: specs, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and a backlog that keeps everyone honest about what is actually shipping. Nobody hands you a ticket queue you did not write yourself.

The problem you'll be solving A corporation with 100,000 employees has thousands of expensive operational problems, and somewhere out there a startup has already solved most of them. Getting those two facts to meet is slow, political, and mostly attempted in spreadsheets that die in someone's downloads folder.
GlassDollar OS is the venture clienting platform that makes it repeatable: sourcing the startups, matching them to real problems, running the pilots, and rolling out what works across the whole organisation. Enterprise customers run real innovation budgets through it. What you scope this month decides what they can do next quarter.

What we´re looking for You have personally written the tickets. 
3+ years in a product company, where scoping and ticket-writing were actually your job rather than something you handed off.
You are technical enough to argue with engineers. 
AI models, API contracts, estimates, sequencing. You push back with reasons, and you change your mind when the reasons coming back are better.
You can write. 
A spec is a piece of writing. We will ask for a sample where the reasoning is visible, polish second.
You write specs worth acting on. 
The valuable ones pull three threads together: where the product is going, what clients are actually telling us, and the knowledge already sitting in the team. You gather all three before you write, so what lands on the board is specific enough to build and pointed enough to matter.
You know what looks good. 
You have a great sense of design and what feels good for users. We will ask you to build a prototype with AI and illustrate the specs visually.
You have worked somewhere small enough that there was nowhere to hide. 
No layers between you and the consequences of a bad spec.
You want to be coached hard. 
Direct feedback, weekly, on your actual work. You will scope alongside the product lead until you are doing it alone, and the goal is that this happens fast.
You are fluent with AI tooling, day to day. 
We want to see the workflow, not hear it described.
You want the scope to grow. 
The people who do best here end up owning areas outright: the major initiatives, the roadmap arguments, and the questions everyone else brings their doubts to. That is earned, and it is genuinely available.

What you`ll do Your job: turn validated opportunities into work an engineer can start on Monday. 
- Turning opportunities into scoped, sequenced, estimable work: specs, acceptance criteria, edge cases, dependencies
- Running the backlog: grooming, prioritisation input, keeping the board honest about what is in flight, blocked, or quietly drifting
- Being the interface between customer signal (support threads, CS conversations, call notes) and the engineering queue
- Coordinating releases and checking that what shipped matches what was scoped
- Presenting product decisions to varied stakeholder groups, from engineers to enterprise clients

What you'll be scoping over your first year: 
- Deep integrations into our customers' organisations. Their systems, their data, their identity stack. This is the work that turns GlassDollar from a tool people visit into infrastructure they run on.
- Public REST APIs and MCP servers , so our customers' engineers and their AI agents can build on top of us.
- AI embedded across the product , inside the surfaces people already work in.
- Workflow automation inside the platform , so the work that used to take six meetings and a shared spreadsheet runs itself.
You will need to understand each of these well enough to write the spec and defend it in the room.
This is a doing role rather than a people-management one. Mid-to-senior individual contributor.

Requirements - 3+ years in a product company, where you personally wrote the tickets
- Technical enough to understand a data model, an API contract, and estimation
- Demonstrable writing ability, be ready to share a spec, PRD or decision doc
Nice to have: - B2B enterprise SaaS background
- Familiarity with venture clienting, corporate innovation, or startup-scouting workflows
- Notion fluency

Don't check every box? Apply anyway. We care more about the questions you ask about a brief than the answer you land on.

How we hire Straightforward. Respectful of your time. No mystery steps.
- Intro call: a quick chat to see if there's a match
- Interview with the PM, including a brief introduction to the work sample : a spec, PRD, or decision doc where your reasoning is visible, plus examples of problems you've framed
- Interview 
- Offer: if it clicks, we don't wait around

Your role will be to: - Run the experiment loop: hypothesis, spec, launch, readout, ship or kill. Keep a steady cadence of live tests.

You are the right fit for the role if you: - Have 3+ years of product management experience, including consumer mobile apps at scale.

- Have a proactive, independent way of working, with leadership and ownership you can point to - not only ideas, but things you shipped. 

- Are a clear communicator and a strong collaborator, with excellent written and spoken English.

- Like hard problems and stay with them until they are solved.

Passion for languages: 

We’re a team of 30 people speaking 20 languages fluently between us. For those wanting to improve their German (or Denglisch!), you can join one of our German classes on us.

As a Tandem team member, we’ll give you a budget for up to 6 “Deep Dive Days” per year. Pick a topic you’ve always wanted to explore for your professional development that has never made it out of your backlog. Then book a cabin in the woods or whatever matches your individual learning style. 

Teams who train together, stay together:

It takes a team to Tandem:

Balance matters: 

Life isn’t just about work. We know when to snooze Slack notifications, recharge our batteries, and take time out for our personal hobbies. As home office has become the new normal for some of us, it’s even more important to be able to switch off from work and relax. 

Modern family:

Relocation without the stress: 

If you’re looking to relocate to Berlin, we’re ready to assist you with the infamous German bureaucracy. Many of us have been through it before, so we have plenty of tips to share. You’ll feel settled in no time.

Reporting to the Senior Director & Lead Managing Counsel, Privacy, Regulatory & Compliance, you will independently advise on complex regional matters, help operationalize evolving legal requirements, and partner closely with Privacy, Product, Engineering, Security, Commercial Legal, Government Affairs, and business teams across Europe. You will play a central role in scaling practical, risk-based privacy and AI compliance frameworks for CoreWeave’s cloud infrastructure, products, and European operations.

- Provide regional guidance on data subject rights, records of processing, privacy notices, consent and cookies, retention and deletion, data sharing, direct marketing, and other core privacy program requirements.

- Advise on European product launches, market entry, strategic partnerships, customer and vendor arrangements, and commercial terms involving privacy, data use, AI, and regulatory responsibility.

- Support cybersecurity and privacy incident response in Europe, including assessment of regulator and data subject notification obligations, engagement with relevant stakeholders, and documentation of defensible legal decisions.

- Lead or support responses to inquiries, audits, consultations, and investigations involving European data protection authorities, AI regulators, and other governmental bodies; coordinate with local counsel and drive follow-up and remediation.

- Develop and maintain regional policies, procedures, playbooks, training, control mappings, and evidence of compliance, and monitor emerging legal and enforcement trends to inform business strategy and program priorities.

- Qualified to practice law in an EU member state or the United Kingdom and in good standing with the applicable professional body.

- Strong working knowledge of the GDPR and UK GDPR, including controller and processor obligations, privacy-by-design requirements, data subject rights, international transfers, DPIAs, security and breach notification, and regulator engagement.

- Meaningful experience with AI governance or emerging AI regulation, including the ability to interpret and operationalize the EU AI Act for technology, cloud, infrastructure, or enterprise use cases.

- Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex regional matters, identify material risk, present practical options, and make clear, defensible recommendations in ambiguous situations.

- Experience building or operationalizing privacy and AI compliance programs through policies, assessments, controls, training, governance processes, monitoring, and audit-ready documentation.

- Technical fluency and the ability to understand data flows, cloud architecture, product functionality, AI systems, and security practices and translate them into actionable legal guidance.

- Excellent drafting and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex legal requirements clearly and influence technical, commercial, and business stakeholders across jurisdictions.

title: Member of Technical Staff
description:
About Seamflow 

Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.

Where we are: 

- Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

- $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed , co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

- Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team 

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role 

A Product Engineer owns the surfaces people actually work in. A coordinator planning a month of inspections across a fleet of auditors. A reviewer signing off on a technical file. These are dense, stateful workflows where the interface carries real consequences, and where the person using it has done the job for twenty years and will know immediately if the software doesn't understand it.

You own product surface end to end: the interface, the backend that supports it, and the data model underneath. Every customer runs the work differently, so there's no template to fall back on. You decide what the right thing to build is, build it, and are the one who hears about it when it's wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for 

We care far more about raw engineering strength than about matching a list of technologies. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, C++ or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, speed and standards are not.

What we're actually screening for:

- You've built something hard and put it in front of real users. Not a prototype, not a course project. Something that ran, broke, and got fixed.

- You build genuinely good interfaces , and you can go as deep on the backend as the feature requires.

- You can hold a complicated workflow in your head and find the version of it that's simple enough to ship.

- Speed with taste. You ship fast, and you're opinionated about what not to build.

- You go to the source. You'll read the customer's actual documents, join the actual call, and look at hundreds of real outputs.

Signals we like, none of them required: 

founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, early engineer at a startup with a serious engineering culture, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup, design sense you can defend, open source you genuinely maintain.

This is probably not for you if 

- You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

- You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

- You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get 

- Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

- Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

- Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

- Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

- A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

title: Team Assistant
description:
📈 Who We Are: 

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. 

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

🚀 The Role

We're hiring a Team Assistant to our CEO and CCO.

tem is rebuilding the energy transaction - transparent, fair and built on trust. Behind that mission are two co-founders whose days generate a heavy volume of admin, and the Executive Business Partners who keep them focused on the right things. You're the layer that keeps it all running.

This is a horizontal Team Assistant role, working closely with our CEO and CCO's Executive Business Partners to make sure the co-founders' day-to-day admin needs are met - inbox support, calendar management, travel, meeting prep and a steady stream of ad-hoc requests. It's not a role about picking up admin as it lands: you'll build the processes, templates and AI automations that make this layer work, and shape how it's done as tem scales. You'll also own the admin and culture layer around our Battersea office - organisation, invoices and team socials, online and offline.

In your first 12 months, you might:

- Take ownership of the BAU admin layer for our two co-founders, working hand in hand with their Executive Business Partners.

- Spot the recurring patterns behind one-off requests and turn them into repeatable processes, templates and AI automations.

- Make the Battersea office a great place to work - organised and running smoothly day to day.

- Build and run a calendar of team socials, online and offline.

- Bring a point of view on what should be automated, delegated or dropped across the admin layer, and make the case for it.

🛠️ Responsibilities

- Keep the day-to-day running: handle BAU admin for our CEO and CCO - inbox support, calendar management, travel and meeting prep - working closely with their Executive Business Partners.

- Turn requests around fast: pick up ad-hoc asks - PA-style requests, event admin, rescheduling - and see them through to done, with proactive follow-ups so nothing sits unactioned.

- Build the operating system: own how this layer of admin actually works, not just the tasks inside it - spot the pattern behind a one-off request and use AI to turn it into a process, template or automation that closes the gap for good.

- Improve as we scale: bring a point of view on what should be automated, delegated or dropped - what works today won't necessarily work in a year, and you'll see it coming.

- Own the Battersea office: keep it organised and running well day to day - office calendar, post, and invoices sent and paid on time with our accounts team.

- Bring people together: plan and run team socials, online and offline.

- Extend the layer: pick up ad-hoc requests from other Executive Business Partners across the exec team.

✅ Requirements

Must-Haves 

- You've supported multiple C-suite executives before, and done it well.

- Process-driven - you spot gaps before they become problems, and automate the fix with AI rather than plugging it manually every time.

- You genuinely enjoy admin - you find creativity in it, and get satisfaction from seeing execs' weeks run smoothly.

- AI-native - comfortable using AI to absorb a high volume of admin work without dropping things. Not just asking it questions, but building processes and skills with it.

- High discretion handling sensitive personal and business information.

- Calm under pressure, comfortable juggling shifting priorities without dropping things.

Desirable 

- Previous startup experience.

- You've partnered with Chiefs of Staff or Executive Business Partners before, so you know what it takes to work together across an exec's operations.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

- Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

- 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

- Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

- Up to £1,200 per year for your remote setup.

- Up to £150 per month for wellbeing.

🤝 Interview Process

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

- Intro call with our Talent team, 30 minutes.

- Skills interview, 30 minutes.

- Practical task - 3 days to complete in your own time.

- Task review interview, 60 minutes.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. 

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

🚀 The Role

We’re hiring a Head of FP&A into our Finance team.

You’ll own tem’s planning and forecasting layer: the financial model, monthly performance vs plan, and the forward-looking view - including cash runway - that leadership and the board run on. Your work is how every part of tem knows how it’s tracking against plan.

This is much more an FP&A job than a controller job. You’ll take the actuals and build your own independent view - modelling, comparing, challenging - partnering closely with the VP of Financial Performance.

In your first 12 months, you might:

- Take full ownership of tem’s financial model and make it the single source of truth for planning.

- Stand up a monthly performance vs plan cycle that lands on time for every part of the business.

- Own the monthly cash runway forecast update with the VP of Financial Performance.

- Build a forward-looking KPI set that leadership actually runs on.

- Own quarterly an annual planning on behalf of Finance

- Codify planning logic into agent-assisted workflows instead of manual spreadsheet grind.

🎯 Responsibilities

- Own the model: take full ownership of the financial model - structure, assumptions, upkeep - so its outputs are trusted across the business.

- Run performance vs plan: deliver the monthly cycle for every part of the business on time, with independent variance analysis built from the actuals.

- Keep the forward view sharp: own the monthly cash runway forecast and maintain the forward-looking KPIs that guide decisions.

- Turn variance into action: translate the numbers into insight leadership can act on.

- Build with AI: codify planning logic into repeatable, agent-assisted workflows so the function scales without headcount.

✅ Requirements

Must-Haves

- Proven FP&A experience - you’ve owned a financial model and a monthly performance vs plan cycle before.

- A background in a complex business: fintech, energy, or any business with a trading element (commodities and oil & gas count).

- A real understanding of financial markets.

- An independent operator: you take raw actuals and build your own view rather than waiting to be handed analysis.

- Excellent data analysis skills: you like getting to the bottom of what drives performance, you’ve worked with messy data, and you relish a tough data challenge.

- Comfortable building AI and agent-assisted workflows into planning processes.

Desirable

- Energy sector experience.

- Scale-up or VC-backed company experience.

- Experience supporting board reporting and investor conversations.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

- Competitive salary - our current band for this role is up to £120,000 or equivalent in local currency.

- Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

- 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

- Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

- Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,200 per year for your remote setup.

- Up to GBP150 or EUR150 per month for wellbeing.

🤝 Interview Process

- First call with our Talent Team.

- Behaviour Interview with the Hiring Manager.

- Technical Interview with the Team (90 mins). You’ll meet with potential peers in this session and will discuss financial modelling, performance vs plan, and forecasting in a business like ours.

- Bar Raiser Interview with Stakeholders.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

🏅 The Role 

Rosso is tem's core IP. It's the transaction infrastructure that replaces what a traditional trading desk does — forecasting energy prices and volume, building a real-time picture of the portfolio, optimising the fees placed on every quote, and autonomously managing hedging decisions. All of it running continuously. All of it on the critical path for every deal tem closes.

Machine learning is at the heart of it. Rosso combines forecasting, optimisation and classical ML to process billions of data points and drive thousands of automated decisions a day. Every inference shapes the prices our customers see.

We've proved the concept. tem now serves 2% of the UK market. The next step is building a pricing engine that doesn't just react — one that proactively drives growth by targeting the right customers at the right time, at the right price, while protecting margin and portfolio balance. Then taking that internationally.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to own pricing ML within Rosso. This is a hands-on senior IC role with real technical authority — you set the strategy, define the mathematical approach, build the models, and ship them. You work closely with MLOps and software engineers, but you don't wait on them. The hard part of this job is the formulation, not the infrastructure.

🚀 Responsibilities 

- Own the technical direction for pricing ML. Define what to build and how. Set the roadmap for the pricing engine as a core piece of tem's IP — and be accountable for its performance.

- Formulate and solve the pricing problem properly. The mathematical foundation doesn't fully exist yet. Your first job is to define it: a dynamic, real-time system that simultaneously optimises for signing probability, portfolio balance, and margin. Choose the right approach — stochastic programming, reinforcement learning, classical ML, or a hybrid — based on the problem, not familiarity.

- Build and ship models end-to-end. Own the modelling and data layer. Write production-grade Python. Architect models with deployment in mind and carry them through to production — you can execute without being blocked by engineering dependencies.

- Solve imbalance problems. Develop probabilistic models to optimise risk management and short-term balancing decisions in a highly dynamic environment.

- Be the voice of pricing ML across the business. Commercial, product, and engineering teams depend on this engine. They need to understand what it's doing and why. You make that happen — clearly, without losing precision.

🎯 Requirements 

Must-haves: 

- Deep experience building ML systems for pricing, revenue optimisation, or real-time decision-making — at companies where pricing is the product, not a supporting function. Track record of models that reached production and moved commercial metrics.

- Strong foundation in stochastic optimisation and probabilistic modelling. The judgement to formulate ambiguous business problems mathematically before reaching for a tool.

- First-principles reasoning across methods. You choose between stochastic programming, reinforcement learning, classical ML, or a simple heuristic based on what the problem demands.

- The engineering depth to match your modelling. Production-grade Python, high bar for code quality, and the ability to carry models from formulation to deployment without being blocked.

- Senior technical leadership. A track record of setting direction for a significant technical area, influencing cross-functional teams, and translating complex model behaviour into clear terms for commercial, product, and engineering stakeholders — so decisions are understood and acted on.

Bonus points: 

- Experience with real-time pricing at scale — ride-hailing, food delivery, logistics, or similar environments where latency and portfolio effects matter.

- Familiarity with energy markets, power trading, or portfolio risk management.

- PhD or equivalent research depth in a quantitative discipline — statistics, applied mathematics, operations research, or similar.

- Ability to reason about trade-offs between optimisation solvers (Gurobi etc.) and gradient-based methods (PyTorch etc.), and the judgement to know when to reach for each.

- Experience with causal inference or reinforcement learning in applied commercial settings.

✨ Benefits & Perks: 

- Salary: Competitive salary — we are looking to pay £150,000 or equivalent in local currency.

title: Senior Producer
description:
Senior Producer

ScapeWorld Entertainment 

Remote. Our working day runs on CET, wherever you sit. Full time, on a long-term contract. Starting as soon as you can. Where you live while you do is up to you; the location field on this posting only fits one country, so please read this as the real rule and apply from wherever you are.

About us 

We are Scape, a Swedish game studio of about 30 people, fully remote by choice. We are launching Scape on Steam Early Access later this year: a growing platform of multiplayer games where a player's identity carries across all of them. The first game inside Scape is Gravity: a precision climbing game where 100 players share one server, one tower, and one long way down. Our senior team has shipped and run live games at studios including Arrowhead (Helldivers 2), Avalanche Studios, Epic and Ubisoft.

Since we are a small team about to put our first game in front of players, we are looking for the person who holds the plan, the priorities and the team together while we do it. If that sounds like you, we would love to meet.

The role 

Let us start with the studio you would be joining. Around thirty people, fully remote, and a group of strong leads in design, art, engineering, QA, community and commercial who own their crafts and run their own teams. What we do not have is the person who looks across all of them at once, holds the plan they are all working to, and makes the day-to-day calls that keep it moving as one. That is this role. It is the only production seat in the company, and it comes with real authority.

You would work closely with the Creative Director. They own what the game is, set the direction and make the big bets. You own the plan that gets us there and the decisions inside it: scope, sequencing and trade-offs within a milestone are yours to make, and you decide which questions need to reach them and which do not. They should be able to step back and know that things are being handled, because they are.

In practice, it comes down to four things:

You know how a game gets made. You can see what depends on what, where the effort really sits, and whether an estimate is going to hold. When a lead tells you how long something takes, you know how to hear it and what has to land for the work to ship on time.

You own the plan and the priorities. Not just the schedule, but the order of work behind it. When two things compete, you decide, or you get the decision made and tell everyone affected. Open questions have an owner and a date. Nothing sits unanswered because nobody was sure whose call it was.

You plan ahead. Problems get found while they are still cheap, and everything that has to land together lands together: builds, assets, store material, localization, press dates.

You lead the team's delivery. People know the plan is real, feel good about hitting it, and are still standing when it ships. The leads lead their crafts. You lead how it all comes together, and you meet each team where it is: some want you in the weeds with them on estimates and sequencing, others mainly need the picture across teams kept current. You read which is which.

We have a production pipeline that works, and like any pipeline it can always be better. You would inherit it as it is, get to know it and the people who run it, and then improve it where you see the need. Nobody here expects you to arrive with all the answers. We do hope you arrive curious about how we work and comfortable telling us, kindly and clearly, where we could do better.

What you will own 

- Production priorities day to day: the order of work across the studio, the trade-off calls within a milestone, and every open question that is blocking someone. You find who can answer, get it answered or escalated with a clear recommendation attached, and close the loop with the teams waiting on it. If a question is blocking someone, it is yours until it is not

- Keeping design, art, engineering, QA and marketing in step with each other, week by week, so nobody is working against a version of the plan that has moved

- The forward view: every feature in flight, what each one is still waiting on, the handoffs between departments caught early, and risk seen while it is still cheap, named, and carrying a mitigation before it turns into a schedule event

- The team's delivery health: sustainable pace, morale, and delivery on target, treated as one problem rather than a trade-off

- Marketing as a real production dependency, and the alignment dates around release: builds, assets, store material, localization drops, press dates, landing on time and together

- The production plan behind all of it: a milestone schedule with a baseline, a forecast per milestone from velocity against remaining scope, estimates held against actuals, and replanning on a cycle rather than after something breaks

- QA in step with everyone else. Our QA lead owns testing; you make sure QA knows what is coming and when, that testable builds land when the plan says they do, and that the QA window sits in the schedule where it belongs rather than where it ends up

- External production partners: localization, video, 3D, anything we outsource. You own the relationship and the communication in both directions, and you chase. Briefs and context going out, deliveries coming in and landing in the build, and the schedule that keeps them in step with everyone else. Leads should never have to chase a partner themselves. The craft stays with the partner; making it fit is on you

- The production process itself and the tools it runs through. We use Jira, including Jira Plans for planning months out against a baseline, and you own it for the studio. You also support hiring managers through their recruitment processes, so a lead who is hiring can focus on assessing the person rather than running the process

You 

Most people who can do this job have around five years in games production behind them. Take that as a description of who tends to apply, not a bar we hold. If you can show us the things below with less, please apply anyway. We would rather meet you than miss you.

- You know how games get made across disciplines: what waits on what, how long things really take, and where a plan is optimistic before the dates say so

- You have produced across several titles and taken at least one PC title all the way to release, including the closing stretch: feature lock, bug burn, submission, the go decision. Which store matters less than that you have been through a PC launch. Projects that were cancelled along the way still count; we know how the last few years have gone for a lot of good people

- You have owned priorities, not just a schedule. You have made cut-or-keep calls on a shipped title and lived with them, and you can tell us about one you got wrong

- You have worked closely with a founder, studio head or creative director, and you know how to take decisions off their plate without going around them

- You have built and driven a schedule, and you have written down a way of working that other people picked up and used. We would love to see examples, in whatever form they exist

- You have led a team to a target without burning it out, and the people on it would work with you again

- You are proactive by default and you work independently. You do not wait to be asked or chased; given an assignment, you find out what it needs and finish it well without someone checking each step. That is what senior means to us

- Leads tell you how things are really going, because you talk with them directly and they trust you with the real picture

- You are fluent in Jira at the level of owning it for a team, Jira Plans included. It is a tool, not the job, but it is the tool we run the plan through, so we need you good with it

- You work our day, which runs on CET; where you sit while you do is up to you. And you are comfortable working in English, written and spoken

Helpful, not required 

- Steam specifically: Steamworks, builds and depots, the store page, review and submission, and how Early Access behaves through the whole run

- Live operations and a patch cadence

- Working with external production partners before, on either side of the relationship

- Time at a small studio where you were the only producer, or where the producer and product owner were the same person

- A remote-first team

What we offer 

The whole project and the authority that comes with it. Real decisions, not just a schedule to report against. Strong leads beside you rather than under you, and a Creative Director who wants to hand things over and means it. A company small enough that what you do is visible in what we ship, and people who will notice.

We are a self-motivated team, remote by choice and flexible in how we work, and we run on people helping each other rather than watching each other. Everyone here is trusted to own their part and supported when they need a hand, and we would like that to be true for you from your first week.

And we are early. Scape is heading to Steam with everything still ahead of it. Joining now means building something with a real chance of becoming big, and being one of the people it belongs to when it does.

Practical 

- Remote. Our working day runs on CET and this role keeps it.

- Full time, on a long-term contract.

- Start: as soon as you can. Tell us your notice period in the application form and we will work around it.

- Recruitment is ongoing.

- Work in a team of cyber threat analysts, economists, data scientists, actuaries and risk modelers to develop insights, scores, and features for a suite of products delivering cyber risk analytics to the (re)insurance industry

- Own CyberCube's point of view on technology risk including factors such as:

- Offensive capabilities and trends among threat actor classes, and validating CyberCube models against observed real-world events,

- Security hygiene standards (e.g. NIST CSF, CIS) and mitigations for companies to lower their potential likelihood and/or impact of events, and

- Technology adoption and trends including the adoption, reliance on and governance of artificial intelligence

… translating these factors into the assumptions and scenarios that drive risk models – especially where historical data is limited

- Working fluency in Python / R, SQL, flat files and complex data types (JSON, XML), APIs, and Excel – enough to specify and interpret analysis with Data/Analytics teams

- Ability to translate real-world cyber threat behavior into modeling assumptions and scenarios – e.g. scenario likelihoods, severity, and mitigation impacts

- Intellectual curiosity, willingness to learn new skills, and push ideas forward

- Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

- Strong communication and consulting presence with key stakeholders

- Experience working in and leading project teams

- Ability to work in an agile, fast-paced startup environment

- Ability to think creatively and respond to emerging threats (cyber, AI, other) and their modeling implications in a timely manner

- Experience with analytics and risk modeling

- Experience in a SaaS product development environment

- Familiarity with ML techniques and statistical data analysis

- Familiarity with AI / LLM risk and its implications for cyber risk, social engineering, product safety, errors/omissions, and critical infrastructure

Most of our growth so far has happened in England. This role owns all three.

It is a genuinely blank page. You work out what winning looks like in each nation, then build the repeatable way to do it, selling everything from a single practice subscription to a health board wide agreement.

- Winning the technical argument: these deals are frequently won or lost on integration. You will hold your own with eHealth teams, IG leads and national bodies on clinical systems, APIs, deployment routes and assurance, without waiting for an engineer to join the call.

- Turning pilots into contracts: generating credible local evidence and then converting it into paid, scaled agreements rather than letting it stall as a permanent trial.

- Using data to pick your battles: building the territory model from list sizes, usage, adoption and pipeline data, and using it to decide where a national deal is realistic and where practice by practice is the faster path.

- Building the playbook: leaving behind documented, repeatable go to market approaches per nation, so this patch scales beyond you.

- You are a proven deal-closer with a track record of carrying your own number and consistently hitting it.

- You are comfortable at both ends of the deal size range, equally credible on a quick practice level close and a twelve month, multi stakeholder board negotiation.

- You are not put off by complexity, whether that is clinical systems, interoperability, deployment routes or information governance. You treat it as part of the sale, not someone else’s problem.

description:

We are a team of 210+ passionate, product-driven people who love solving big challenges. Backed by top investors like 500 Startups and Surface Ventures, we are building one of mobile's fastest-growing SaaS companies and aiming for number one worldwide.

Why This Role Matters

Flow Builder is one of Adapty's core products and the biggest bet we're making right now.

Our customers use it to assemble the screens their users see before paying: onboarding, quizzes, paywalls, and post-purchase experiences. They build multi-screen flows with branching, variables, and conditional content directly in the browser. The Adapty SDK renders those flows natively on iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, and Capacitor, and a change published in the editor reaches users without an app release.

We're building the most capable native-rendering builder on the market, and that sets a high bar for engineering. - Skilled in integrating and adapting external IPs such as GPIOs, LVDS, SPI/I²C interfaces; experience with high-speed serializers/deserializers (SerDes) is a highly valued plus.

And you get a head start few revenue leaders are ever handed: distribution through OVHcloud's platform and customer base — yours to build and exploit as you see fit.

- Customer success & expansion. Own net revenue retention and expansion.

- Forward-deployed engineering . Turn FDE into a core lever of the sales strategy — embedded in deal strategy and closing — and build out a complete catalog of service offerings around it.

- Process audit. Audit every commercial process end to end and instrument the funnel that makes the whole engine measurable and predictable.

- Leading the team. Managing & scaling a high-ownership international revenue org distributed across Paris and New York.

Who you are 

- 10+ years in B2B revenue leadership, with a track record of scaling a company through a comparable ARR band

- You've personally carried and closed complex enterprise deals — and you're credible with technical buyers (CTOs, engineering and product leaders), not just procurement.

- At ease across the full deal spectrum — from self-serve and SMB transactions to six- and seven-figure enterprise contracts .

- Experience selling into both private and public sectors, comfortable with the longer cycles, procurement and compliance the latter demands.

- You've owned more than sales: you've run or worked hand-in-glove with customer success and partnerships, and you grasp the role solutions / forward-deployed engineering plays in landing technical accounts. This role spans the full revenue org, so a pure sales background isn't enough.

Bonus points

title: Brand Designer, AI + Ops
description:
About Gladia 

Gladia builds the audio AI infrastructure behind the new generation of voice products. Our mission is to give every voice platform true conversational intelligence — the audio infrastructure that understands every conversation, turning voice into the world's most valuable data layer. 

Our API turns real-world conversational audio into accurate, structured, real-time output — powered by our proprietary Solaria ASR , across 100+ languages, with industry-leading latency.

Hundreds of companies build their voice products on Gladia — from meeting assistants and voice agents to sales-enablement and contact-center platforms. We started in Paris, our growth is developer-led and heavily US-driven (and we're going after the US market hard).

Headquartered in vibrant tech hubs like Paris and New York City, Gladia has been by OVH Groupe — Europe's leading cloud provider — and now operates as a fully autonomous brand and company within the Group. 

We're guided by four values :

- Honest — Say the real thing, kindly.

- Smart — Work smart, ship fast.

- Builders — Own your scope, build to last.

- Caring — Support people, take pride in the craft.

The role 

AI is at the core of our product — and increasingly at the core of how we design. Our brand runs on a custom system that's prompt-driven and code-native. The depth of this role is in scaling it, keeping our identity sharp and consistent across every touchpoint, extending it into video, and supporting our growing set of internal products.

That means working with a high degree of autonomy. You anticipate needs, reach out directly to the teams you support without waiting to be briefed, and you've already run a brand on your own — comfortable managing external partners when needed, and used to moving fast.

It also means strong web skills are non-negotiable: our website is hand-coded (Next.js, HTML, CSS) in Cursor and hosted on Vercel, so comfort with Cursor or an equivalent IDE is a prerequisite, alongside real fluency and curiosity around AI tools.

What you'll do 

- Own Gladia's brand identity end-to-end across our website, marketing materials, decks, and video

- Design and build our website directly in code (Next.js, HTML, CSS), working in an IDE like Cursor and shipping through GitHub, deployed on Vercel

- Operate and extend our AI-powered design system, using prompting as a core creative tool alongside traditional design craft

- Push our web presence toward richer, more immersive and interactive experiences

- Extend our visual identity into new formats, in particular video

- Contribute design support to internal tools such as GladiaFlow and Compare STT

- Move fast and deliver independently across a wide range of formats

Who you are 

- Senior brand design experience, ideally at a startup, having owned a brand end-to-end rather than executed against an existing brand book

- A portfolio that shows systems thinking: a cohesive identity with real range across web, video, decks, and brand — not a handful of one-off pieces

- Fluency with Cursor (or an equivalent IDE), confident enough with code to review and ship changes via GitHub

- A real, hands-on relationship with AI tools in your design workflow — genuine daily use, not occasional dabbling

- The ability to build a distinct visual language for a technical, abstract product, without leaning on stock photography or literal product screenshots

- Sharp, fast decision-making, with the ability to clearly explain the reasoning behind your choices

- Fluent English

Bonus Point 

- Experience managing external vendors or freelancers

- Background in B2B SaaS or deep tech, where the product itself is hard to visualize

- Based in or open to working on-site in Paris, as a big plus

What Gladia Offers 

- The compensation offered is based on seniority and experience, and would typically range from 65K to 85K base salary 

- Hybrid work from our offices in the heart of Paris (no compulsory office days)

- Lunch vouchers (approx. 200€/month)

- An allowance of 300€ for the adaptation of your workstation

- Health insurance (100% coverage) and a pension contract for you & your family

- Flexible vacation policy

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Embedded AI
description:
Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)? Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy? Are our Engineering principles aligned with your vision? Then Pennylane is the right place for you!

Our vision

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones). We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while giving them access to the key financial information they need to make the best decisions for their business.

About us

Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon in Europe!). In 5 years of existence, we've managed to:

- 💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

- 💰 Raise a total of €400 million, including from Sequoia — the famous Silicon Valley fund that invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe and Paypal

- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1,000 happy Pennylaners, and earn a place among the greatest companies to work for in France (and remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor

- 🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities and a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of employees already work from all parts of Europe

- 🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms, with outstanding ratings

- 🚀 Reach more than 1,000,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6,000 accounting firms using Pennylane in France

WHY this position is of utmost importance to reach our mission 

Pennylane is becoming the financial OS of European SMEs and accounting firms. A growing share of the work done inside our product will be automated or assisted by AI. Our strategy operates at three layers: verticalized AI embedded in the product, an agent interface that makes Pennylane readable and actionable by AIs, and the Pennylane orchestrator agent itself.

The Embedded AI team owns the first layer. We build the specialized machine learning systems behind Copilot and Autopilot : invoice parsing, document classification, accounting suggestions, matching, scoring, Bookkeeping Autopilot and Revision Autopilot.

Models are commoditizing fast. What makes the difference is our ability to frame the right problem, use Pennylane’s data and accounting knowledge, evaluate quality on real workflows, and operate reliable systems in production.

By joining us as a Machine Learning Engineer — Embedded AI , you will turn difficult accounting problems into trusted ML products used every day. You will combine strong ML engineering, product thinking and production ownership to improve both automation and user trust.

HOW you will contribute as a Machine Learning Engineer — Embedded AI 

You will join the Embedded AI team within our ML & AI organization. The team works closely with product squads and accounting experts, from initial exploration to production, monitoring and continuous improvement.

- You will design and ship ML systems for document understanding, extraction, classification, matching, ranking, scoring and recommendations.

- You will contribute directly to our Copilot and Autopilot experiences, including Bookkeeping Autopilot and Revision Autopilot.

- You will own the full lifecycle of your solutions: problem framing, data and labeling strategy, baselines, training, evaluation, deployment, experimentation, monitoring and maintenance.

- You will turn user corrections and production failures into better datasets, models and product behavior.

- You will define quality metrics that reflect real user value: precision and recall, automation coverage, straight-through processing, human correction rate, latency and cost.

- You will partner with Product, Engineering and accounting experts to understand workflows, define what “correct” means and integrate ML naturally into the user experience.

- You will choose the simplest reliable approach for each problem — deterministic logic, classical ML, deep learning or generative AI — rather than starting from a preferred model.

- You will help improve our shared ML engineering practices: reusable components, experimentation, observability, data quality and reliable training and inference pipelines.

- You will stay ahead of the curve by monitoring emerging ML and AI techniques — including multimodal and generative models — and applying them when they create measurable value.

WHAT you can expect from your life at Pennylane 

Within one month: 

- You will learn about Pennylane, our users, our accounting workflows and our AI vision during onboarding.

- You will get familiar with our ML stack, production systems, datasets, metrics and ways of working.

- You will meet your product and engineering partners and contribute to a first scoped improvement.

Within 3 months: 

- You will own an Embedded AI use case end to end, with clear offline and production metrics.

- You will have shipped a meaningful improvement to a Copilot or Autopilot capability.

- You will be comfortable with our technical stack, including Python, Pytorch, PySpark, Redshift, Airflow, AWS SageMaker and our monitoring tools.

- You will use real user feedback and error analysis to prioritize the next iterations.

Within 6 months: 

- You will lead larger cross-team ML projects and help shape the Embedded AI roadmap.

- You will improve the reliability, automation coverage and maintainability of one or more production systems.

- You will share best practices and raise the bar for ML engineering, evaluation and production ownership across the team.

And beyond: the ML & AI teams will continue growing with the company 

This means opportunities to mentor new team members, lead major product initiatives and help define the technical standards that make trusted AI possible at Pennylane.

Who are we looking for? 

You may be a great fit if you:

- Have 5–8 years of experience and are very strong in Python.

- Have hands-on experience building and operating machine learning systems at scale in production — not only training models or running notebooks.

- Know how to frame an ambiguous product problem, establish a baseline and select useful metrics before optimizing a model.

- Have strong experience in several of these areas: document AI, NLP, classification, ranking, recommendation, anomaly detection, deep learning or generative AI.

- Care about data quality, observability, failure modes, cost and long-term maintainability as much as model performance.

- Have a balanced blend of technical, business and product skills, and communicate well with software engineers, product managers and non-technical domain experts.

- Are fluent in English; French is not mandatory.

Nice to have:

- Experience with accounting, fintech or other high-trust business workflows.

- Experience with human-in-the-loop systems, active learning or learning from user corrections.

- Experience running ML systems at scale with strict latency, reliability or cost constraints.

- Familiarity with multimodal or generative models for document understanding.

What does the recruitment process look like? 

- A first interview with our Talent Acquisition Manager

- A case study interview covering problem framing, data, modeling, evaluation, deployment and monitoring (75 min)

- A past project interview to discuss your experience and technical decisions (60 min)

- An interview with our Tech & Product leaders to discuss our company culture (30 min)

Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer & gérer un vivier de candidats. You may object at any time and request the deletion of your data by writing to Learn more

Pennylane verarbeitet Ihre Daten, um Ihre Bewerbung zu bearbeiten und Ihre Eignung für die Stelle zu beurteilen. 🎯 Ton rôle 

Tu rejoins l’équipe Support applicatif et technique en tant qu’expert métier et plateforme.

Tu es l’interlocuteur privilégié des dirigeants, des comptables internalisés et des cabinets d’expertise-comptable qui utilisent Pennylane pour gérer leur comptabilité et leurs finances.

Au quotidien, tu analyses leurs problématiques, les accompagnes dans la résolution de leurs demandes et les aides à tirer pleinement parti de la plateforme. Tu contribues également à l’amélioration du produit en faisant remonter des retours structurés aux équipes internes.

Support et résolution de problèmes 

- Réceptionner, qualifier et analyser les demandes des utilisateurs

- Comprendre leur problématique et leur contexte métier

- Assurer le suivi des tickets jusqu’à leur résolution complète

- Escalader les sujets complexes aux équipes techniques ou produit

- Garantir un haut niveau de qualité de service

Accompagnement des migrations 

- Aider les comptables en entreprise et en cabinet à intégrer leurs données dans Pennylane

- Comprendre les enjeux liés à la migration depuis un autre logiciel comptable

- Identifier les éventuelles difficultés et coordonner leur résolution

- Participer à l’amélioration des processus et de la documentation associés

Amélioration continue et partage d’expertise 

- Créer et mettre à jour les supports d’aide destinés aux utilisateurs

- Identifier les questions récurrentes et favoriser l’autonomie des clients

- Partager tes connaissances comptables avec l’équipe

- Faire remonter les irritants et les besoins aux équipes produit

- Proposer des améliorations sur les process et les outils internes

🚀 Tes premiers mois chez Pennylane 

Les 3 premiers mois 

- Tu suis la Pennylane Academy et te formes sur le produit et les process de l’équipe

- Tu découvres l’entreprise, sa vision et ses différents départements

- Tu apprends à identifier les parties prenantes et à collaborer efficacement

- Tu commences à traiter des demandes liées à la comptabilité

Entre 4 et 6 mois 

- Tu gagnes en autonomie et prends en charge tes demandes de bout en bout

- Tu traites des problématiques de plus en plus complexes

- Tu contribues aux supports d’aide et au partage de connaissances

- Tu deviens un relais de la voix du client auprès des équipes produit

Tu deviens progressivement un expert produit et métier, capable d’identifier les axes d’amélioration et de porter des projets. Des évolutions vers des sujets Support plus complexes, la gestion de comptes ou la mise en œuvre de Pennylane sont également possibles.

🙋 Le profil que nous recherchons 

- Formation comptable : BTS CGO, DCG, BTS Assistant de gestion PME-PMI, Bachelor Responsable administratif et comptable, Master CCA ou équivalent

- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience en cabinet d’expertise-comptable

- Idéalement, au moins trois périodes fiscales réalisées

- Une expérience en contact direct avec des dirigeants est un plus

- Solides connaissances des principes comptables et de la réalité des cabinets

- Appétence pour les outils numériques et les nouvelles technologies

- Autonomie, curiosité et capacité à résoudre des problèmes

- Excellentes qualités rédactionnelles et pédagogie

- Sens du service et aisance dans la relation client

- Capacité à travailler en équipe et à s’adapter rapidement

- Envie d’apprendre et de suivre les évolutions du produit

- Anglais professionnel (compréhension écrite, orale et expression écrite)

- La connaissance de Pennylane est un plus

- Un premier échange avec un recruteur, 30 minutes

title: Senior Legal Counsel – Contracts (German speaker)
description:
Could your legal expertise help build the contractual foundations of Europe’s next financial management platform? 

At Pennylane, we believe legal should be more than a safeguard. It should be a business enabler.

Our ambition is to equip millions of small and medium-sized businesses across Europe with a complete, high-performing financial management platform. As Pennylane continues to grow rapidly in France and expand internationally, we are looking for a Senior Legal Counsel, Contracts to join our Legal, Compliance & Risk team.

Within a Legal department of 10 professionals, the Contracts team secures Pennylane’s commercial and operational relationships with customers, suppliers, partner firms, resellers, integrators and strategic partners.

Reporting to the Lead Legal Counsel, Contracts , you will work closely with our Sales, Partnerships, Security, Finance and Product teams. This is a hands-on role where legal rigor, creativity and business pragmatism are equally valued.

🌍 What is Pennylane? 

Pennylane is one of France’s most dynamic fintech companies, currently expanding rapidly across Europe.

In just six years, we have managed to: 

💻 Establish ourselves in the market as an innovative provider of accounting and financial management software

💰 Raise a total of €400 million from renowned investors, including Sequoia, Silicon Valley’s leading venture capital firm, known for backing Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, PayPal, and many others in their early days

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 co-founders to a team of 1,000 employees, with an average Glassdoor rating of 4.9/5 and 94% of reviewers saying they would recommend Pennylane to their friends and family

🌍 Build an international team made up of employees from 25 different countries, with a truly flexible remote-working culture

🚀 More than 900,000 small and medium-sized businesses and over 6,000 accounting firms in France already use Pennylane!

🎯 Your role 

You will act as a trusted legal partner for teams across Pennylane, managing a broad range of commercial and operational agreements from drafting through to signature and post-signature follow-up.

You will also help make our contracting processes more efficient and scalable, contributing to the tools, templates, playbooks and legal culture that support Pennylane’s growth.

📋 Your responsibilities 

International contracts 

- Draft and negotiate purchase orders and related agreements with partner firms, primarily outside France, with a current focus on Germany.

- Manage contracts with strategic international suppliers.

- Maintain and improve templates in line with regulatory, product and business developments.

- Work with Sales and Partnerships to streamline the contracting process.

Customer, reseller and integrator agreements 

- Improve customer terms and conditions for SME customers across France and Europe.

- Support Sales with the contracting process and automated quotations.

- Review and negotiate agreements with Pennylane integrators and resellers.

- Anticipate the contractual impact of key regulations, including e-invoicing, payment services and the EU AI Act.

- Contribute to contract templates and playbooks.

Legal operations and collaboration 

- Structure and improve internal contracting processes to increase efficiency and scalability.

- Optimize our contract management tools, including Tomorro, Pivot and Notion.

- Identify opportunities to automate repetitive, low-value tasks, including through AI.

- Provide clear, pragmatic advice to Sales, Partnerships, Finance, Security and Product teams.

- Train non-legal teams and help build a strong legal culture across Pennylane.

🙋 The profile we are looking for 

- You are a qualified lawyer or legal counsel with extensive experience in contract law, gained in a law firm, particularly in IP/IT, technology or SaaS, and/or in a fast-growing tech company.

- You are fluent in English and have a working knowledge of Franch and German.

- You have strong expertise in B2B SaaS agreements , including IP, indemnification, liability caps, SLAs and data-related provisions.

- You are autonomous and comfortable managing matters from start to finish.

- You have experience working in a multi-jurisdictional environment, particularly across France and Europe.

- You are interested in legal operations and technology, and have experience structuring processes or optimizing contract management tools.

- You are a genuine business partner , able to help teams move quickly while protecting the company.

- You are rigorous, concise and able to make complex legal topics clear to non-legal audiences.

- You enjoy building in a fast-moving environment where ambiguity, prioritization and rapid iteration are part of the job.

This role is available in a hybrid format from Paris or as a fully remote position elsewhere in France or Germany
