title: Software Engineer - Data (All Genders)
description:
Hey! Imagine amateur football finally had the platform it deserves. Every weekend, millions of people write their own personal football stories – on pitches, in clubs and on the sidelines. We believe this passion deserves a digital home too. That's exactly what we're building every single day. 

tl;dr We’re looking for someone to help make our Teamwear business scalable beyond its current scope - building the data infrastructure, pipelines and tools that power the next stage of Teamwear.

Main information - Start: Immediately
- Location: Cologne, Berlin London or Remote
- Workload: Full-time
- Team: Teamwear/Tech

Is this a match? The most important basics – so we both know if it could work.
- 100% remote: This role is generally available 100% remote within the EU or UK. If you'd still love to work from one of our offices in Cologne, Berlin or London - you're more than welcome.
- Experience: You bring 6-8 years of experience in software engineering and data engineering.
- Languages: You speak English fluently - German is a big plus.
- Startup spirit: You'd rather shape things than just tick boxes - even when that means figuring stuff out without a finished roadmap.

What you'll do - your playing field This is how you move our mission forward every day.
- Data Pipelines: You build and maintain data pipelines for automated data collection, structured so that new sources and markets can be added quickly.
- Algorithms: You develop algorithms to extract relevant information from websites and images.
- Data Quality: You ensure data quality through validation, confidence levels, monitoring, and clean handovers internally and to partners.
- Data Infrastructure: You manage and further develop the data infrastructure of the Teamwear area.
- Technical Point of Contact: You act as the second technical point of contact for the Teamwear area.
In addition to your core responsibilities, you will also:
- Internal Tools: You develop internal tools that enable the team to collect and correct data themselves.
- Analytics & Reports: You create analytics and reports for internal stakeholders and external partners.

What you bring to the team We're not looking for a perfect CV. But you should recognise yourself in these points.
- Broad Technical Skillset: You move between data pipelines, backend and some frontend, and are not afraid of AI or image analysis.
- Data Automation: You have experience with automated data pipelines, web scraping and image processing.
- Databases & Data Modelling: You have expertise in databases and data modelling.
- Independent Working: You work independently, even when there is no second engineer in the room and the context comes from business teams.
- Fast Learner: You quickly get familiar with unfamiliar domains and ask the right questions along the way.
- 80/20 Mindset: You know when fast and good enough is the right approach and when the data needs to be 100% accurate because a decision is based on it.
- Data Quality: You care about details when it comes to data quality and make uncertainties explicit.
- Data-Driven Thinking: You don't stop at analysing the data. You identify what is in the data, what it means and what we should look at next - even if nobody asked.
- Engineering Practice: You write clean, maintainable code and follow good engineering practices such as testing and code reviews.
- Tools: Python, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Grafana, Metabase, Pulumi, Kubernetes, AWS, LLM APIs
Good to know 
We want you to know what this role really looks like from day one.
- If you are looking for clearly defined tickets, a large engineering team and a finished tech stack, this role is probably not for you. - You will work largely as a team of two within Engineering. Most of your day-to-day work will be with business people, not engineers.
- You have two connections: technically to Engineering and on the content side to the Teamwear team. This gives you a lot of freedom and means you need to set your own priorities.
- A large part of the role is data collection and data quality, rather than greenfield ML. The exciting part is turning messy, real-world sources into reliable data.
- The area is new. There is no finished setup for you to work with - you will help build it.
- AI-first: We work AI-first, and AI tools are an active part of our workflow.

Bonus Not a must - but this'll definitely earn you extra points.
- Experience with AWS, Kubernetes or IaC (Pulumi/Terraform). You can also learn this with us.
- Experience presenting and preparing data for non-technical audiences.
- A personal connection to amateur football.

The Prematch Setup We want you to love joining us - and still love being part of the team a long time from now. - Be part of it from the start – Shape how Prematch grows and transforms amateur football.
- Competitive salary – You’ll be paid fairly and transparently.
- Employee participation (VSOP) - directly benefit from the company’s success.
- Three cool offices in Cologne, Berlin, and London - true startup vibes to work and grow together. Want to visit another office? We support that too!
- Remote work - depending on your distance to the office, you work 1–3 days a week onsite and the rest flexibly remote - whatever suits you best. Tech & Product roles sometimes offer 100% remote.
- Remote, even from afar - Whether it’s a week of sunshine abroad or a few days with family - we allow flexible work from outside your usual location.
- Team spirit - whether in the office or at home, we use cool tools and a virtual office to keep the team tightly connected.
- Modern IT equipment - We provide the tools and devices you need to be productive.
- 27 vacation days per year - For your rest and to recharge. Plus special arrangements if you’re a parent, so you can better balance family and relaxation.
- Team events at our locations - Whether after work in Cologne, Berlin, or London: we regularly bring teams together to connect and grow stronger.
- Offsites with the whole team - Four days out of the daily grind with the entire team: trips, brainstorming, onsite collaboration, and real team spirit.

Still here? Sounds like a pretty good match. If you've made it this far, we hope we've managed to show you one thing: how we work, what we believe in and why this role at PREMATCH is something special. Maybe this is exactly the moment you've been waiting for: a team that thinks big, a vision that actually moves things and the chance to help reshape amateur football digitally – together with us. Now it's your turn. - Click on ‘Apply now’ - it’ll only take 2 minutes.
- All we need is your CV. You can tell us the rest in our simple, short application form.
- Don’t meet all the requirements? If you think you’re still a good fit - just apply

What you’ll do 

We build Qodana to bring the intelligence of JetBrains IDEs directly into the CI/CD pipeline, helping engineering teams spot security flaws, license issues, and bugs before they ever reach production. As AI-assisted coding grows, the need for deep, static code analysis is more critical than ever.

In this role, you’ll join our Qodana Core team to expand our static analysis engine and design new algorithms for complex, inter-procedural code analysis. You will have direct ownership over how we configure and orchestrate these analyses across different environments. You’ll collaborate closely with other JetBrains compiler and IDE teams, directly influencing how development teams worldwide maintain code quality and adopt AI safely.

Day to day, you will: 

- Design and implement new static analysis checks, rules, and inter-procedural analysis algorithms.

- Extend Qodana’s capabilities in critical areas like license compliance, security, and vulnerability detection.

- Optimize how code analysis runs, configure execution paths, and orchestrate performance based on project context.

- Build and refine CI/CD integrations to make Qodana easy to adopt across different development workflows.

- Collaborate with compiler and IDE teams across JetBrains to share insights and align analysis engines.

- Take ownership of features from early concept to release, gathering feedback and iterating to make them better.

- A deep curiosity about code structure, compilers, and how static analysis works.

- Comfort working in a distributed team across different countries and time zones.

- A focus on quality over quick fixes, valuing long-term maintainability in your work.

title: Senior Software Developer (JCP Core Foundation Licensing and Quotation)
description:
If you want to build and own the systems that decide what JetBrains customers are entitled to use and bill them accurately for it, this is for you. You will focus on designing backend services, keeping complex commercial flows correct, and tackling hard distributed systems challenges on the critical path of every paid request.

About JetBrains 

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do 

At JetBrains, the Cloud Platform department builds the underlying infrastructure that powers authentication, paid capabilities, usage metering, and accounting. Within this department, the Licensing & Billing team sits right at the center of our commercial model, turning what a customer buys into what they are actually allowed to use, and accounting for that consumption accurately enough to bill on.

The complexity of our entitlement, quota, and metering systems continues to grow. In this role, you will own the correctness and evolution of these backend services, take full ownership of end-to-end data flows, tackle distributed consistency across unreliable upstream systems, and ensure revenue-affecting data migrations happen cleanly without taking services offline.

Day to day, you will: 

- Design, build, and operate backend services that decide what a customer is entitled to and what their usage costs.

- Own flows end to end, from ingesting licensing and purchase data from upstream systems to enforcing quotas and recording consumption.

- Evolve our domain model to handle new commercial structures, combining seat-based plans and usage-based models.

- Design integrations with external systems, ensuring correctness through idempotency, ordering, reconciliation, and eventual consistency.

- Plan and execute live data migrations using feature flags, dual writes, backfills, and verification at every stage.

- Build observability into our systems by defining invariants, metrics, and alerts to catch silent divergence before customers do.

- Design internal APIs with explicit focus on versioning, backward compatibility, and developer experience for other JetBrains teams.

- Improve system performance and reliability under continuous production load while decommissioning legacy subsystems.

- Write integration tests against real dependencies and maintain reliable test infrastructure.

- Investigate production incidents, find root causes, and follow through on lasting fixes.

What you’ll bring 

- An engineer’s dedication to accuracy, especially in domains where system errors have direct financial impact.

- Pragmatic judgment when designing distributed systems where correctness under unreliable delivery is the main constraint.

- A habit of trusting metrics, traces, and logs to understand production behavior rather than relying on assumptions.

- Comfort navigating and simplifying large existing codebases containing legacy decisions.

- Clear, direct communication skills to agree on API contracts across teams with different priorities.

- A focus on testing as an essential design tool rather than an afterthought.

What you’ll need 

- A proven track record of building and operating backend services on the JVM platform using Kotlin or Java.

- A solid working knowledge of relational databases, including transactions, isolation levels, locking, indexing, and live schema migrations (PostgreSQL preferred).

- A deep understanding of distributed systems patterns, such as idempotency, retry strategies, eventual consistency, and data reconciliation.

- Practical experience making live data migrations or system changes without downtime using feature flags and staged rollouts.

- Experience designing versioned, backward-compatible APIs for other engineering teams.

- Hands-on experience with event-driven architectures and message brokers like Kafka.

- The ability to diagnose, debug, and resolve production incidents in complex environments.

- Proficiency in both written and spoken English.

What success looks like 

Success in this role means building a bulletproof entitlement and metering foundation that product teams can trust without hesitation. You will have successfully migrated live commercial systems to support new billing models without downtime or data divergence. Silent errors will be caught automatically by system invariants before affecting users, and internal teams will integrate seamlessly with your clean, versioned APIs.

title: Director, Customer Compensation & Policy
description:
About the Role 

Within Global Customer Experience (GCX), our mission is to advance the HelloFresh customer relationship from reactive resolution to proactive, trust-building service. The compensation function sits at the heart of that mission: it is the mechanism through which the business acknowledges failures, restores customer confidence, and, when done well, turns a bad experience into a reason to stay.

The Associate Director, Customer Compensation & Policy is responsible for the global strategy, architecture, and governance of how HelloFresh compensates customers across all markets and brands. This is not a policy maintenance role. It is a strategic function that sits at the intersection of customer economics, operational data, behavioral experimentation, and cross-functional influence.

You will own one of the most financially material and customer-sensitive levers in the business. You will shape a multi-year roadmap and hold peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market Leadership accountable for the quality of inputs that determine how well and how efficiently we recover customer trust.

The ideal candidate brings a rare combination: analytical rigor sharp enough to architect a global compensation engine from first principles, and the executive presence to drive adoption across a complex, multi-market organization without formal authority over most of the people they need to move. 

What You'll Own 

Global Compensation Strategy & Engine Architecture 

- Own the end-to-end strategic vision for how HelloFresh categorizes customer errors and determines compensation across all markets, brands, and contact channels.

- Lead the design and continuous evolution of the compensation engine: along with Tech, you’ll define the the rules, thresholds, segmentation logic, and automation frameworks that govern recovery decisions at scale.

- Define the principles that govern trade-offs between customer generosity and cost discipline and translate those principles into operational rules that hold across market complexity and brand variation.

- Partner with Technology to ensure the compensation engine is scalable, auditable, and capable of supporting dynamic, AI-assisted decisioning as the product evolves.

Experimentation & Behavioral Economics 

- Set the global roadmap for compensation experimentation: A/B testing across offer types, value levels, channel timing, and segmentation variables.

- Apply behavioral economics frameworks to compensation design understanding how recovery offers shape long-term retention, repurchase behavior, and brand perception, not just immediate satisfaction.

- Define the measurement framework for experimentation: what constitutes a successful test, what confidence warrants global rollout, and how results are synthesized into durable policy change.

- Partner with Analytics & Insights to ensure test design, sample integrity, and rollout analysis meet a rigorous standard of evidence.

Financial Stewardship & Cost Governance 

- Own the global compensation P&L line: tracking spend by market, error category, customer segment, and channel — and holding yourself accountable to defined cost-per-incident and avoidable-contact targets.

- Identify and close financial leakage: cases where compensation is being issued without policy justification, at incorrect values, or at the wrong frequency.

- Build the reporting infrastructure that makes compensation economics visible to GCX leadership, market GMs, and Finance — with the granularity and context needed to drive decisions.

- Define the right balance between cost optimization and customer lifetime value investment: not just 'spend less' but 'spend where it earns back.

Fraud Policy & Global Governance 

- Own the global fraud and abuse prevention framework: the policies, detection logic, thresholds, and escalation paths that protect the business without creating friction for genuine customers.

- Lead the governance rhythm for policy: quarterly reviews, market exception management, escalation adjudication, and framework versioning across a multi-brand, multi-market environment.

- Act as the final authority on complex, cross-market policy gaps — resolving ambiguity with speed, consistency, and strategic clarity rather than routing decisions upward by default.

- Maintain global standards while creating principled space for market-level adaptation where local context genuinely requires it.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Stakeholder Accountability 

- Represent the compensation function in senior forums translating customer economics into requirements that peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market GMs must respond to.

- Hold cross-functional partners accountable for the upstream data quality, operational accuracy, and system reliability that the compensation engine depends on.

- Drive adoption of policy changes across markets and brands, building communication and change management plans that make new frameworks land — not just launch.

- Influence at VP and Director level across multiple functions; escalate only strategic blockers, not routine alignment.

What You'll Bring 

Education 

- MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification required.

- Undergraduate degree in Economics, Business, Engineering, or a quantitative discipline.

Experience 

- 8–12 years of progressive experience in customer strategy, pricing, operations, or a directly adjacent domain with meaningful exposure to global, multi-market environments.

- Demonstrated track record of owning a financially significant operational lever and managing it with both analytical precision and strategic judgment.

- Prior experience leading and developing teams; comfort operating as a senior individual contributor and a people leader simultaneously.

- Background in subscription commerce, logistics, or consumer-facing operations strongly preferred. Familiarity with the economics of customer recovery in high-volume, low-margin environments is a distinct advantage.

Technical & Analytical 

- Advanced proficiency in SQL and data analysis; able to build and pressure-test the analytical models that underpin policy decisions without delegating the logic to others.

- Fluency with experimentation methodology: test design, statistical significance, holdout analysis, and the translation of results into policy not just reporting.

- Experience working with or alongside engineering teams to define product and system requirements for rules-based or AI-assisted decisioning tools.

- Comfort with financial modeling: building the business case for compensation investment, forecasting spend impact, and tracking actuals against plan.

Leadership & Influence 

- Senior executive presence: able to walk into a GM, COO, or CFO conversation with a clear point of view, defend it under pressure, and leave with alignment.

- A credible voice with peers and upward stakeholders not because of title, but because of the quality of analysis and clarity of communication.

- Structured and decisive under ambiguity: able to make a defensible call with incomplete information and adjust as evidence develops.

- Genuinely collaborative across markets and functions able to hold people to standards without damaging the relationships needed to sustain them.

What we offer

- Modern and comfortable working space with great co-workers in Berlin-Kreuzberg 

- Discount for HelloFresh boxes and Convini products 

- Development possibilities along with internal trainings and a yearly Learning & Development budget 

- Flexible working hours including Work From Home/Work from Abroad/Sabbatical Policy, as well as a home office set up budget 

- Extensive Onboarding and Buddy Program 

- Social events including team events, Friday beers, company runs, book club, etc. 

- Discounted fitness offers with our Urban Sports Club and John Reed partners and yoga classes 

- Well-being initiatives in cooperation with Headspace and Spill 

- Childcare and company pension scheme benefit 

- Monthly transportation budget via NAVIT

title: Project Engineering Manager - Core Spreads Manufacturing
description:
Location: Pratau, Germany

On-site

About the position 

As a Project Engineering Manager – Core Spreads Manufacturing, you will be responsible for leading, coordinating, and delivering engineering and capital investment projects across the Core Spreads manufacturing network, with a primary focus on the Pratau and Katowice (by travelling) factories. The role is critical to strengthening manufacturing capability by implementing technically robust, safe, compliant, and cost-effective solutions that improve safety, quality, sustainability, reliability, capacity, and overall operational performance. The role covers the full project lifecycle, from initial business needs definition, feasibility assessment, concept development, budgeting, technical design, and supplier selection through installation, commissioning, qualification, operational handover, and post-implementation review. You will ensure that projects are delivered on time, within the approved budget, in accordance with company engineering standards, and in full compliance with safety, quality, food safety, GMP, and regulatory requirements.

You will:

- Lead engineering and capital expenditure projects within the Core Spreads factories, ensuring clear scope, objectives, deliverables, responsibilities, timelines, and governance are established from project initiation.

- Develop and manage project documentation, including business case inputs, user requirement specifications (URS), scope definitions, technical specifications, cost estimates, project schedules, risk registers, procurement packages, commissioning plans, and handover documentation.

- Coordinate engineering design, equipment selection, vendor technical clarification, procurement support, installation planning, construction supervision, commissioning, qualification, and start-up activities.

- Monitor project progress, costs, risks, and milestones, escalating issues where required and implementing corrective actions to ensure delivery against agreed targets.

- Ensure effective project close-out, including completion of technical documentation, training, asset registration, maintenance requirements, lessons learned, and operational handover to site teams.

- Perform engineering assessments, feasibility studies, option evaluations, and technical risk reviews to support investment decisions and project prioritisation.

- Analyse process, packaging, utilities, and equipment performance data to identify opportunities to improve reliability, increase efficiency, reduce waste, improve yield, reduce energy consumption, and optimise costs.

- Lead or support structured troubleshooting activities for recurring technical issues, applying root cause analysis and practical engineering problem-solving methodologies.

- Drive value creation, continuous improvement, and operational excellence initiatives in close collaboration with Manufacturing, Maintenance, Quality, and T&I teams.

- Support the standardisation of technical solutions, equipment specifications, and engineering ways of working across the Core Spreads manufacturing network.

- Work closely with Manufacturing, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Quality, Safety, Procurement, Finance, and T&I stakeholders to ensure project objectives are aligned with business priorities and site operational needs.

- Coordinate external suppliers, contractors, OEMs, and engineering service providers, ensuring clear technical communication, effective scope management, safety compliance, and high delivery performance.

- Prepare clear project updates, decision papers, presentations, budget summaries, risk assessments, and steering committee materials for site and regional leadership teams.

- Facilitate effective communication between sites, functions, and project teams to enable timely decision-making, resource availability, and smooth project execution during factory operations.

- Ensure all project activities comply with company engineering standards, site safety rules, contractor management requirements, food safety standards, quality systems, GMP requirements, and all applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

- Lead or support Management of Change (MoC) processes, ensuring that technical, operational, safety, quality, environmental, and financial impacts are appropriately assessed, documented, approved, and implemented.

- Promote a strong safety and compliance culture by ensuring that appropriate risk assessments, method statements, permit-to-work procedures, contractor supervision, and safe start-up practices are in place.

- Maintain accurate project records and support audit readiness through disciplined documentation, full traceability of decisions, and controlled handover of technical information.

So what does it take to be successful in this role?   

You have a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related field, along with at least five years of experience in project engineering, process engineering, maintenance engineering, or capital project delivery within the food industry or a similarly regulated manufacturing environment. You bring solid knowledge of food processing, packaging technologies, hygienic design principles, operational excellence, and change management practices. You have a strong understanding of engineering project delivery processes, industrial equipment, utilities, process systems, packaging lines, commissioning, and operational handover. You have demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, suppliers, contractors, risks, and cross-functional stakeholders in a manufacturing environment, and are able to balance strategic project objectives with practical factory execution, ensuring technical solutions are reliable, maintainable, scalable, and aligned with long-term site and category manufacturing strategies. You are fluent in both English and German, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn. You are an effective communicator and collaborative team player, open to traveling for project execution, supplier visits, factory acceptance tests (FATs), and on-site activities. Additionally, you are proficient in MS Office and engineering software such as AutoCAD and SolidWorks.

title: Senior Design Engineer, Design System
description:

Why this role matters 

At Celonis, design has to scale across a complex, enterprise-grade process intelligence platform, and increasingly, it has to scale to machines as well as people. AI coding agents now generate a growing share of the UI our engineers ship, and our design system is the contract that keeps that output on-brand, accessible, and consistent.

This role sits at the intersection of design, engineering, and product, with a strong emphasis on craft, usability, and scalability. You'll design and build the system itself, owning interaction decisions and front-end architecture, and translating complex process data and AI-driven behaviors into intuitive, high-performance experiences. It's a senior role: you'll often operate with minimal design oversight, set standards, lead initiatives, and mentor others while staying deeply hands-on in both design and code.

About the team 

You'll join the team that owns Celonis's design system and the operations behind how design gets done. We sit at the intersection of design and engineering, and we treat the system as a living product with real users, internal designers, product engineers, and the AI agents that now consume it.

What you'll do 

- Design and build production components in Angular and TypeScript, our design system is built in Angular and we may adopt React over time, on a foundation of rock-solid HTML and CSS (semantic markup, ARIA, and modern CSS custom properties driving design tokens).

- Own interaction decisions, component design, and front-end architecture end-to-end, independently translating ambiguous requirements into thoughtful, usable UX.

- Translate complex process-intelligence data and AI-driven behaviors into clear, intuitive, high-performance operator experiences.

- Set the technical and craft standard for front-end quality, polish, motion and animation, performance, and accessibility, across the team.

- Drive rapid prototyping to explore novel interaction concepts and turn ambitious design visions into distinctive, testable experiences.

- Collaborate with designers, PMs, and engineers to derive and evolve the design system through a healthy contribution model.

- Make the system agent-ready: maintain tokens-as-code in the W3C DTCG format (Style Dictionary or similar) and structure component metadata, docs, and APIs so AI coding agents can consume them as reliable context.

- Author and maintain Figma Code Connect mappings so Figma components link cleanly to their coded counterparts for engineers and agents alike.

- Build evals as guardrails, visual-regression, accessibility, and token-compliance checks in CI, so generated and contributed UI meets the bar before it ships.

- Use AI tooling daily (Figma Make, v0, Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, or similar), applying senior design and engineering judgment to critique and correct the output.

- Lead system initiatives and mentor designers and engineers contributing to it.

What you'll bring 

- Around 5–8 years across design engineering / UX engineering / front-end, including significant hands-on work building a design system or component library in a SaaS or B2B environment.

- Excellent UX instincts with strong attention to interaction detail and usability, you can own design decisions independently, with minimal oversight.

- Strong production front-end skills in Angular and TypeScript with rock-solid HTML and CSS fundamentals; experience with (or genuine openness to) React is a plus.

- Deep understanding of design token architecture (primitive → semantic → component tiers) and modern token pipelines.

- Strong Figma fluency and comfort moving fluidly between design and code.

- Demonstrated accessibility expertise (WCAG 2.2) implemented in code.

- Hands-on fluency with AI design and coding tools, and an opinionated, responsible point of view on using them.

- A strong product mindset and bias toward ownership, plus the communication and leadership of a senior IC.

Bonus points 

- Experience with Figma Code Connect in production.

- Experience building or integrating MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers e.g. the Figma Dev Mode MCP server or a custom design-system MCP server.

- Experience building evals for AI-generated UI, or writing specs/prompts for AI generation.

- Background working on complex, data-dense, or real-time interfaces (a strong fit for our process-intelligence product).

- Token-pipeline experience with Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, or equivalent.

This is a senior role: you'll own major areas of the system with full autonomy, design and ship with a high bar for craft, set the standards others build to, lead initiatives, and mentor. title: Senior Product Manager, Technical (m/f/d)
description:
About the Company 

Affinidi is a technology company dedicated to changing data ownership for good. We empower businesses and individuals with control and ownership of their data, with a comprehensive approach to managing their holistic identity – accounting for all aspects of their digital footprint while ensuring privacy and security. 

Affinidi’s technology enables users to benefit from decentralised digital identity solutions. We believe that everyone has the right to own and control their data, and we are committed to creating a trusted digital credentials ecosystem that empowers businesses and individuals to securely exchange data and services across borders and industries. 

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager (Technical) who wants to help define how trust is built into the next generation of AI systems. At Affinidi, we’re building the Trust Fabric product suite to give AI agents verifiable identity, policy guardrails, and real-time observability, so organisations can move from promising proofs of concept to secure, governed production deployments with confidence. 

This is a role for builders. You’ll work side by side with engineering to turn ambitious ideas into real, high-impact products, fast, iteratively, and with strong product judgment. You’ll take on complex, ambiguous challenges that don’t come with a playbook, bring structure to what matters, and help the team move with clarity, speed, and conviction. You’ll also collaborate with deeply engaged teams and senior leaders in an environment that expects high standards, values ownership, and gives you the chance to shape meaningful products from the ground up. 

If you like combining technical depth, product thinking, and execution, you’ll fit right in. 

What you’ll be doing 

- Shape and deliver solutions : Partner closely with engineers to define and refine solutions early, helping move ideas from concept to production in practical, incremental steps while staying close enough to implementation to understand trade-offs and guide decisions. 

- Drive focused, outcome-oriented delivery: Balance user needs, market context, and execution speed while focusing on getting working solutions into users’ hands for validation, then iterate based on feedback and measurable outcomes. 

- Work through ambiguity : Take ownership of areas where requirements are not fully defined, structure problems into clear, actionable paths forward, and maintain momentum even as direction continues to evolve. 

- Own product direction: Contribute to product strategy and roadmap definition, align short-term priorities with longer-term platform thinking, and make thoughtful trade-offs that support both delivery and scalability. 

- Collaborate across stakeholders : Work across engineering, design, and go-to-market teams, engage effectively with senior and executive stakeholders, and bring alignment and clarity in environments with diverse perspectives. 

- Be developer-obsessed : Understand developer workflows and key pain points, and help improve integration, usability, and the overall product experience. 

What we’re looking for 

- Core experience : You bring 5+ years of experience in Technical Product Management, a strong technical background that lets you engage deeply with engineering topics, hands-on experience working with APIs, systems, and integrations, and a proven track record of delivering products in close collaboration with engineering teams. 

- Technical depth : You are comfortable understanding how systems are designed and operate in practice, able to engage in technical discussions, challenge assumptions, and evaluate trade-offs, and willing to go into detail when needed by reviewing flows, investigating issues, or clarifying implementation approaches. 

- Mindset : You take ownership from problem to outcome, are comfortable working with ambiguity and evolving priorities, combine structured thinking with a bias toward action, and can move between big-picture strategy and practical execution. 

- Collaboration & communication : You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, are comfortable working with experienced, highly engaged stakeholders, and know how to build alignment and drive decisions forward. 

- Nice to have : It’s a plus if you have had exposure to identity, distributed systems, or similar domains, and experience in fast-paced, product-led environments. 

What you’ll get 

- A team that values ownership, quality, and speed 

- Close collaboration between product and engineering 

- Hybrid working model in Berlin + flexible hours 

- Unlimited vacation 

- Competitive compensation 

- A strong environment to learn, build, and have impact 

Equal Opportunity 

We believe in hiring different and diverse talent and providing a safe space where everyone can share their views without fear, where differences are celebrated, and where no one is left out. Inclusive cultures are the foundation for collaboration and innovation within our team.

By applying for this position, you confirm that you have read and understood Affinidi’s Candidate Privacy Policy , and consent to the collection, use, and disclosure of your personal data for recruitment purposes, as described in the policy .

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
description:
Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth. 

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.

Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands.

About the Role: 

We are looking for a Senior Reliability Engineer with focus on Identity and Access Management (IAM) to join the Corporate Engineering team. As an SRE together with other engineers you will be responsible for the continuous operation, further development and enhancement of Planet’s corporate infrastructure and applications, acting as the technical authority for our enterprise identity ecosystem. 

This is a full-time, hybrid role which will require you to work from our Berlin, Haarlem or Ljubljana office 3 days per week.

Impact You’ll Own: 

- Help to ensure the operation of Planet’s internal IT systems, specifically architecting and maintaining our identity providers (Okta, Auth0, Keycloak).

- Improve existing and create new solutions by engineering automated zero-day Joiner, Mover, and Leaver (JML) workflows directly from our HRIS (e.g., HiBob).

- Scripting & Tooling: Use Python or Go to automate repetitive tasks, build custom provisioning connectors for legacy applications, and enforce identity data minimization.

- Identify and reduce operational toil through automation, making our systems self-healing and predictable.

- Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Leverage APIs, Terraform, Ansible, or SaltStack to manage configurations as code, moving away from manual UI/CLI changes across our identity platforms.

- Participate in an on-call rotation and drive the continuous improvement of incident response, root cause analysis (RCA), and post-mortem processes for complex authentication failures.

- Collaborate closely with Security and other IT teams to embed reliability, scalability, and security best practices from the ground up, ensuring our identity architecture complies with GDPR and Zero Trust principles.

What You Bring: 

- 6+ years experience in infrastructure development and/or operations, with a dedicated focus on Identity and Access Management.

- Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.

- Expertise with a scripting language like Python.

- Track record of working with large web applications or computer clusters and managing complex identity architectures (Okta, Auth0, Keycloak).

- Experience integrating HR Information Systems with identity directories and handling complex edge cases (re-hires, cross-border transfers).

- Solid understanding of Network principles and operations alongside modern identity protocols (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SCIM).

- Practical understanding of PKI, certificate lifecycles (S/MIME, X.509), and managing legacy directories like Active Directory.

What Makes You Stand Out: 

- Operational experience in deploying and maintaining databases.

- Experience using Docker, ECS or Linux Containers in a production environment.

- Awareness of best practices about systems security and defensive programming

- Experience with version control e.g. Git.

- Experience in deploying and maintaining virtual machines e.g. KVM, ProxMox.

- Experience in software development using CI/CD processes and tools e.g. Jenkins, GitLab.

- Experience with Access Control systems, e. g. Avigilon, Verkada or dormakaba.

- Experience with Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and deployment automation, renewal, and revocation of personal S/MIME certificates.

description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . 

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity and we would be interested in applicants based in Spain, Ireland, Germany, the UK or Sweden at this time. 

Senior Backend Engineer - Databases - Loki Query | EMEA | Remote 

The Opportunity: 

Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, and traces with Grafana. It allows our customers to leverage the best open source observability software – including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, and Tempo – without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack

The Databases team owns the telemetry databases that are Mimir for metrics , Loki for logs , Tempo for traces , and Pyroscope for profiles . Our databases are OSS projects that we also offer as a Cloud service supporting Grafana Cloud, and as an on-premise solution. They are multi-tenant distributed systems implemented in Go and running on Kubernetes across all major Cloud service providers (GCP, Azure, AWS). title: Senior Specialist, Employee Relations - EMEA
description:
About Remote 

Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work! 

What this job can offer you

As a critical extension of our clients’ HR teams, we navigate and advise on the intricate paths of global employment with unmatched speed, expertise, and precision. The vision of the Lifecycle team at Remote is not just about maintaining the gold standard in HR practices; it’s about elevating it, integrating cutting-edge technology solutions, and enriching customer experiences in over 80+ countries. On this team, your work directly influences our ability to sustain and extend our compliance coverage, continuously enhance our customer journeys, and significantly increase our operational capacity. Dive into a role where your passion for innovation, commitment to excellence, and drive to make a global difference aligns with our mission to empower organizations worldwide to employ anyone, anywhere — compliantly.

The Lifecycle Specialist, Employee Relations & Transitions manages employee exits for Remote's external employees with a focus on legal compliance and providing delightful customer service. Additionally, the specialist provides first-level Employee Relations support, guiding clients through workplace concerns and coordinating appropriate resources when needed.

As part of a larger employee Lifecycle team, the Specialist is also expected to contribute to process improvements and initiatives in line with Remote's strategic goals and values.

Key Responsibilities

Offboarding

- Manage and resolve end-to-end employee exits across multiple international jurisdictions, prioritizing a superior offboarding experience for Remote's clients and their employees.

- Provide sound guidance and manage clients' requests on various HR matters, including but not limited to termination, resignation and transfer procedures, employment contracts, and redundancy processes, ensuring legal compliance and best practices.

- Lead and facilitate meetings with clients and external employees, including but not limited to workforce reduction consultation meetings, administrative hearings, negotiations in separations and settlements, providing guidance on terminations, and delivering termination outcomes.

- Influence and negotiate positive outcomes in complex terminations, balancing multiple stakeholders with competing interests.

- Liaise with and coordinate various internal and external stakeholders to ensure compliance in offboarding activities and audits, including but not limited to payroll, legal counsel, government bodies, and trade unions.

- Draft, tailor and administer all termination and supplementary documents with accuracy and attention to detail, ensuring employee records are maintained with strict adherence to privacy and confidentiality regulations.

- Process offboarding on Remote's internal HRIS platform, collaborating with various internal stakeholders, such as Customer Success, Legal, Payroll, Benefits, Time and Attendance, amongst other verticals, to ensure all aspects of the employee exit are administered correctly and promptly.

- Be the subject-matter expert and respond to internal and external queries on all offboarding matters in conjunction with Lifecycle's internal stakeholders.

- Navigate clients through Remote's Employee Relations resources and guides, helping them understand applicable policies and processes.

- Conduct preliminary assessment of workplace concerns, identifying key facts and applicable local regulations.

- Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure appropriate handling of employee relations matters.

- Support clients in understanding progressive disciplinary approaches and documentation requirements.

- Monitor ongoing employee relations cases, ensuring timely follow-up and coordination with relevant stakeholders.

- Actively identify opportunities for and contribute to process improvements, automation, product development and overall customer and employee experience through the offboarding and employee relations processes.

- Experience as a HR Advisor or HR Business Partner, with generalist HR competencies and exposure across the employee lifecycle.

- Proven experience with a strong background in managing voluntary and involuntary exits (terminations) with care, sensitivity and legal compliance; and providing comprehensive HR support and guidance on employment laws and regulations, spanning various jurisdictions.

- Ability to interpret and apply industrial instruments, analyze complex HR issues, undertake research, provide practical solutions and effectively communicate recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders when operating in ambiguous and unfamiliar environments.

- Basic understanding of employee relations principles, progressive discipline approaches, and workplace investigation fundamentals.

- Excellent communication, influencing, conflict management, and negotiation skills, with the ability to confidently lead difficult conversations to a positive outcome, often where parties have conflicting interests, maintaining professionalism and strict confidentiality.

- Business-level (advanced) proficiency in written and spoken English, with additional languages considered a plus.

- Aptitude and appetite to innovate and optimize processes, continuously identifying and implementing opportunities for automation and championing best practices.

- Efficiency in operations, with an awareness of the importance of thorough record-keeping and data integrity.

- Tech-savvy, with the ability to successfully collaborate asynchronously on various tools, and adapt to new and evolving systems.

- Ability to work autonomously and cohesively in an international team in a fast-paced, asynchronous, remote environment with multiple priorities. Willingness to work flexible hours as needed.

- Proactive and self-motivated with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.

- Demonstrates strong automation and AI capabilities and AI fluency. 

Practicals

title: Account Executive (AE) | DACH (d/f/m)
description:
About the role

Luminovo builds the B2B SaaS platform that powers the electronics supply chain. DACH is our home market and one of our strongest, and we’re adding an Account Executive to the German-speaking team.

Unlike traditional transactional sales, you'll be selling complex supply chain software to technical buyers—requiring deep discovery, consultative selling, and the ability to prove measurable ROI in a trillion-dollar industry. You'll sell software that directly impacts how electronics companies—from automotive suppliers to industrial equipment manufacturers—manage their complete electronics supply chain. The impact is tangible, the industry is fascinating, and the growth trajectory is yours to shape.

Who you are

- You’ve sold B2B software, and you can walk through your own numbers from memory: quota, attainment, average deal size, how long your ramp took

- You’ve built something that didn’t exist before you — a segment, a first playbook, a function nobody had staffed, a company of your own. You’re more comfortable without a playbook than with an inherited one

- You use AI as more than a better search engine. You’ve built your own automations, workflows, or tools, and you can name what you shipped and what came of it

- You’ve been close to how electronics or physical products actually get made — manufacturing, hardware, or supply chain. A bonus rather than a must, and the strongest single signal we look for, because it’s what lets you find the pain before a customer names it

- You’re consultative by instinct. Our buyers rarely arrive knowing they have a problem worth solving, so short cycles with demo-ready buyers aren’t the motion here

- You work in German and English at a professional level. Discovery, demos, and negotiation happen in German; the company runs in English

Your potential growth path: 

- Months 1-6: Master the product, close your first 5-10 deals, build your DACH network

- Months 6-18: Take on larger deals, navigate complex stakeholder environments, mentor BDRs

- 18+ months: Transition to Enterprise AE (€100k+ deals), own strategic accounts, mentor junior AEs

Your performance objectives 

📣 Generate pipeline 

- Build your network. Connect with 50+ relevant decision-makers at electronics manufacturers per quarter through industry events, LinkedIn, and targeted outreach. Establish Luminovo's presence at 2-3 key industry fairs annually.

- Generate qualified pipeline. Create €240k-€400k in qualified pipeline ARR per quarter (depending on seniority) through outbound prospecting, events, and inbound lead qualification using SPICED discovery.

- Qualify with precision. Run customer-centric discovery to uncover Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical event, and Decision criteria. Quantify potential value before investing in lengthy sales cycles.

💪 Close opportunities 

- Inspire with demos. Deliver product demonstrations tailored to each customer's pain points. Clearly articulate our competitive positioning.

- Prove measurable value. Collaborate with domain experts to run workshops that demonstrate ROI through concrete impact calculations (time savings, cost reductions, efficiency gains).

- Close strategically. Guide prospects through complex buyer journeys, map stakeholders, and turn negotiations into win-win outcomes. Close €60k-€100k in new ARR per quarter (depending on seniority) with smooth handovers to Customer Success.

💡 Build expertise 

- Become an industry insider. Develop deep knowledge of electronics supply chains and feed customer insights back to product teams.

- Master consultative selling. Make SPICED your guiding principle and build expertise in technical SaaS sales with longer cycles and multi-stakeholder decisions.

📈 Lead by example 

- Own your metrics. Monitor pipeline health, conversion rates, and deal velocity. Use data to consistently hit quarterly targets.

- Enable your peers. Mentor junior AEs through shadowing and deal reviews. Contribute to our sales playbook.

- Embrace feedback. Reflect on every major customer interaction and proactively seek coaching to maximize impact.

🇪🇺 Your territory 

You'll primarily cover the German-speaking market (DACH), with some English-speaking territories. Fluency in 🇩🇪 German and 🇬🇧 English is essential.

📍 Work location 

Munich headquarters or Berlin satellite office (both in hybrid setup with home-office flexibility). Our sales team meets in the office three days per week. Occasional travel for team retreats and industry events (expenses covered).

Whom you'll be working with 

- Clifton Lobo , VP Global Sales — Your manager who'll coach you on deal strategy and career progression

- Sebastian Schaal , Co-Founder — Provides strategic guidance on positioning and pricing

- Inga Schwarz , Team Lead and Pioneer AE for OEM — Your primary partner in building the OEM sales playbook

- Max Hungenbach and RevOps — Provide CRM support, dashboards, and sales enablement

- Marketing, Customer Success & Product teams — Regular collaboration on campaigns, customer onboarding, and product roadmap

💡 Skills, knowledge, and expertise 

Just so you know—we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. We care much more about your motivation and ability to help us accelerate technical progress than we care about your CV.

If you're interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles—see here .

⚡️ About Luminovo 

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry . 

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress. 

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain. 

To date, over 300 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million .

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things 

As a remote-first company headquartered in Munich, our brilliant team is spread across cities including Munich, New York, Austin, Calgary, Berlin, London, Valencia, Nairobi, and Verona, among others. 🌍

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. Among us are graduates from institutions like Stanford University and the University of Cambridge, as well as talented individuals with unconventional CVs. What matters most is their drive to build great things.

We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

title: Workday Financial Systems Architect
description:
Hi! We are AMBOSS and we are looking for a Financial Systems Architect to join our team, and shape the future of medical education with us!

About AMBOSS 

AMBOSS is a dynamic learning and clinical decision support tool committed to empowering medical professionals globally to deliver optimal care. Since our inception in 2012, we've harnessed cutting-edge technology to transform the way physicians acquire and apply scientific knowledge. Each AMBOSSian is passionate about being the champion of clinicians today - this motivates and unites us each day towards success. And what does success look like? When a clinician or med student tells us, “AMBOSS makes practicing medicine easier and enjoyable. I love what I do, and a big part is because of AMBOSS.”

Want to learn more about our culture? Watch our video to explore what makes us unique.

Why Systems at AMBOSS? 

AMBOSS runs on a growing landscape of business systems: Workday as the ERP at the center, connected to Stripe, HubSpot, Pleo, Avalara, our banks, payroll and archiving. The Systems team, part of Data & Systems, makes this landscape develop as a whole: every problem solved in the system where it belongs, and processes that run smoothly from order to cash and from purchase to payment. Our expertise is platform-independent: accounting logic, process design, integration patterns and systems thinking. Working side by side with Finance, Accounting, Commercial, Data and IT, we support AMBOSS in pursuing its mission: empowering medical professionals worldwide to provide the best possible care.

Why can this position be exciting for you?

You are the technical owner of Workday Financials at AMBOSS: you take the tenant over from our implementation partner and run it. Some days that means a configuration fix before the close, other days the design of a new integration or the assessment of a new module.

You are the expert and advisor for everything Workday. Our Business Systems Manager owns the roadmap, stakeholder coordination and partner management and works with you day to day.

This is a senior individual contributor role: you build and own Workday the way a senior engineer owns a production system. It is not an administrator role with a ticket queue.

Where we are 

Workday Financials goes live in November 2026 as our ERP for three entities in Germany, the US and Italy. Around twelve integrations connect it to the rest of the landscape, and they are the most demanding part of it. You join during hypercare and the first closes in Workday, with the first year-end close and statutory audit ahead.

You will: 

- Own the tenant technically. Configuration and business processes across record-to-report (General Ledger), procure-to-pay (Accounts Payable), order-to-cash (Accounts Receivable) and bank connectivity (Banking & Settlement), the security model and the financial data model.

- Take over from the implementation partner. Review, document and harden what was delivered, close the gaps and bring run responsibility in-house as early as possible after go-live. Where we still use consultants, you set the technical standard and review their work.

- Own the Workday side of every integration. Design and build the EIBs, Core Connectors, Studio integrations, web services and RaaS reports behind each interface and agree the interface contracts with our Data Platform engineers, who build and run the pipelines around the tenant.

- Advise Accounting and Finance. Translate requirements into system design, say clearly what Workday can and cannot do and advise where in the landscape a problem is best solved.

- Run it like a production system. Tier 2/3 support with root-cause fixes, testing discipline (unit, regression, UAT), the two Workday releases a year and a change log with configuration documentation. You enable the accounting stream leads who handle first-line questions.

- Build the reports, dashboards and calculated fields that Finance and leadership rely on, and make them self-serve where possible.

- Be the technical expert on expansions. HCM, treasury, automated VAT reporting and global payroll off DATEV: assess feasibility, design the solution and configure it.

You bring: 

- Workday Financials depth. 5+ years hands-on, including at least one full implementation and the post-go-live ownership of a tenant (hypercare, first closes, releases).

- Configuration expertise. Core modules (GL, AP, AR, Banking & Settlement), the business process framework, configurable security and the financial data model (FDM, worktags).

- Reporting. Custom and matrix reports, calculated fields and BIRT.

- Systems thinking. Experience connecting SaaS business systems (APIs, integration patterns) and the habit of thinking in end-to-end processes across tools.

- Accounting understanding. Chart of accounts, period close, reconciliations and audit requirements.

- Engineering mindset. Structured troubleshooting to the root cause, disciplined testing and documentation that others can use.

- Communication. Excellent English: precise with engineers, plain with finance colleagues.

Nice to have: 

- Hands-on experience with Workday integration tooling: EIBs, Core Connectors, Studio, web services, RaaS and XSLT

- Proficiency in German

- Workday Pro certification in Financials or Integrations

- Multi-entity, multi-currency or multi-GAAP experience (IFRS alongside local GAAP); experience with tax and e-invoicing platforms such as Avalara

- Accounting Center, Prism Analytics, Extend or Orchestrate

- A Workday consulting or CoE background

- A formal accounting background (degree, CPA or equivalent) or experience with internal controls and SOX in a Workday context

You enjoy: 

- Owning a system end to end. Taking over a freshly built tenant and knowing it better than anyone else in the company within months.

- Depth you can explain. You do the hard configuration and integration work yourself, and you explain the result to accountants and engineers in language each of them understands.

- Getting the details right where they matter. Financial systems punish sloppiness: a misconfigured business process or a broken integration shows up in the books. You can tell a load-bearing detail (audit trail, data integrity, reconciliations) from polish that can wait.

- Working like an engineer. You bring testing, documentation and versioned change into Workday and use modern tooling, including AI assistants, to move faster. When a release or a new module moves the ground, you question your own setup first.

What success looks like after your first year: 

- The tenant runs without the implementation partner.

- The integrations run reliably through every month-end and year-end close: data lands in Workday without manual intervention, and monitoring catches failures before Accounting does.

- The first year-end close and statutory audit in Workday are done with you answering the auditors' system questions, and two Workday releases are handled end to end.

- Accounting and Finance treat you as the expert and advisor for everything Workday: requirements are shaped with you from the start, and your call on how a process should run in the system is the one they act on.

Benefits: 

🌴 Rest & Time Off (30 paid vacation days, AMBOSS holiday, personal purpose day and more)

🥙Food & Office Comfort ( Daily healthy breakfast & lunch by in-house chef in Berlin HQ, AMBOSS daycare, work remotely from other office spaces in Cologne, Sardinia, Cape Town)

🏃 Health, Fitness & Mobility (Urban Sports Club -M plan- , Fitbit Versa 3, Deutschland Ticket…)

title: Chief Technology Officer
description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist , NPR , TED , and The Washington Post . We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. 

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do . If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Priority application deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Early applications are heavily encouraged.

We’re growing at incredible speed, and expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. We’re hiring a Chief Technology Officer to lead the building and rebuilding of the technology, systems and ways of working that will enable a sustained $5B+ p/a operation.

You will build software that safely and securely moves billions of dollars to millions of vulnerable people in some of the poorest and highest need parts of the world. This will require applying excellent engineering, team building and organizational judgment to complex, high-stakes operations: identity and fraud management, machine learning on large but imperfect datasets (cell phone data, satellite imagery, government registries), mobile money integrations, low-connectivity environments, rapidly evolving requirements all in diverse regulatory environments and country contexts. You’ll need to keep our legacy technology stack stable and performant, while in parallel building new systems from the ground up for our next level of scale.

You will lead engineering, data, security and enterprise technology – with a small, mighty and rapidly growing engineering team of ~15, and the expectation that this can at least double to ~30 in the next 12 months if you want it to. You’ll report to a CEO with deep experience running technology companies, and partner with our VP Product.

This role is remote, with working hours between US Eastern Time and East African Time, and some preference for candidates in our office hubs of New York, London, or Nairobi.

What we’re looking for: 

- An exceptional hirer, manager and organizer of technical talent. Proven record identifying, hiring, developing and retaining excellent engineers and engineering leaders, and creating team processes that consistently deliver software with quality and velocity.

- Deep technical judgment, applied close to the work. You can evaluate major designs, pressure-test architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, and recognize when a team is heading the wrong way, without becoming the primary implementer. Low-ego: you’ll investigate a problem yourself when that’s what the situation requires.

- Business judgment and decisiveness under ambiguity. You’re not just a technical leader, you’re also a business executive. You understand the business, are a strong cross-functional partner, and have a history of good judgment when navigating tradeoffs of long vs. short term, speed, reliability, security, flexibility, cost, technical quality, and user impact.

- AI first. You have a point of view on where AI meaningfully changes engineering productivity and organizational capability, and you’ve moved a team from experimentation to real, measured use. You can set the tools, culture, goals, and guardrails that leverage the opportunities and mitigate the risks of an AI first engineering culture.

- Embody and set an example for GD values. We take our values incredibly seriously, and expect our leaders to embody, nurture, and promote them in the way they work and the teams they build.

- Advantages, not requirements. Experience in an operationally complex or regulated domain (fintech, payments, humanitarian response, global development); systems involving financial controls, fraud risk, identity, or sensitive recipient data; operating across multiple countries, particularly lower-income or infrastructure-constrained ones; leading both modern product engineering and enterprise technology.

What you’ll do 

- Define our technology vision and target stack. Own the technical strategy for technology-first delivery at $5B+/year: architecture, platforms, build-vs-buy, and what we retire. Work with executive, product, finance, risk, and data leaders to turn program and product strategy into a sequenced, credible portfolio of technical investments.

- Balance a demanding portfolio. You'll manage six workstreams that all matter and won't all move at once: (1) building our new cash delivery stack (remote-first verification, fraud prevention, massive volume) (2) stabilizing our legacy stack until switchover, then managing the migration; (3) donor-facing fundraising products; (4) our global emergency cash system (and eventual white-labelling of that product); (5) enterprise technology; (6) internal tooling, platform, and cybersecurity. Deciding sequencing and staffing across these (and saying "not yet" credibly) is the job.

- Build and grow an exceptional technology organization. Recruit outstanding engineering and technology talent, design the org GiveDirectly needs at its next stage of scale (engineering, product, data, security, infrastructure, enterprise systems), and create the accountability, decision rights, and career paths to sustain high talent density. Grow the engineering team from 15 to ~30 with a lean but durable management structure.

- Own the technical direction and quality bar. Guide consequential decisions on integrations, data, security, reliability, and technical debt. Ensure our systems can safely support a major increase in transaction volume, geographic reach, and organizational dependence on technology. Set a pragmatic quality bar appropriate to high-stakes financial delivery while preserving speed.

- Lead across organizational boundaries. Serve as a member of GiveDirectly’s executive team, reporting to the CEO and bringing technology into major strategic and operating decisions. Help non-technical leaders understand technical constraints and costs, build credibility with country and functional leaders by understanding their realities, and force clarity when priorities, ownership, or tradeoffs are ambiguous.

- Travel. Approximately 4–6 trips per year, including visits to GiveDirectly countries of operation.

We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy so pay is consistent across comparable roles.

- Bonus: $45,000-$112,000 (bonus is % based and decided based on org-wide performance, we will share full methodology during the hiring process)

- Annual Benefits Stipend: ~$21,000

If you are not based in one of the countries listed above, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Working at GiveDirectly

title: QA Automation Lead [gn] Data Intelligence
description:
The QA Automation Team is the ultimate guardian of our platform’s reliability, scalability, and deployment velocity. In a complex, data-heavy ecosystem, manual testing is a bottleneck; continuous, intelligent, and bulletproof automation is the only way forward.

We are looking for a QA Automation Lead who will architect, scale, and own our automated testing strategy end-to-end. You are not a passive test-case writer or a mere script executor; you are a highly technical, proactive engineer who thrives on breaking complex distributed systems, designing robust testing frameworks, and enforcing a culture of absolute quality. You will lead a dedicated team of automation engineers, embed quality gates directly into our CI/CD pipelines, and use data-driven metrics to eliminate regressions before they ever reach production.

Core Responsibilities:

- 
End-to-End Testing Infrastructure: Design, scale, and maintain robust automation frameworks capable of testing the complex SaaS and distributed data architectures of the Actian Data Intelligence Platform.

- 
Pipeline Integration: Embed automated test suites seamlessly into the CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions/Jenkins) to achieve true continuous integration and rapid feedback loops.

- 
Advanced Testing Topologies: Move beyond basic UI testing. Drive deep integration, API, performance, resilience, and data-integrity automation across the entire product stack.

- 
Technical Anchor: Act as the ultimate technical authority for the QA automation squad, establishing clean code standards for test scripts, conducting rigorous code reviews, and minimizing framework technical debt.

- 
Upskilling & Accountability: Coach junior automation engineers and guide functional QA testers in transitioning toward automated practices, ensuring everyone owns their automation targets.

- 
Resource Optimization: Allocate engineering capacity effectively across feature testing, framework enhancement, and technical debt reduction.

- 
Release Gatekeeper: Own the final quality sign-off for platform releases. Have the technical authority and conviction to halt deployments if quality thresholds are not met.

- 
Cross-Functional Bridge: Collaborate closely with Product Management, Core Engineering, and DevOps to understand new features early, mapping out automation strategies before the code is written.

- 
Defect Triage Collaboration: Partner with the Sustaining Engineering team to analyze production leaks, quickly writing automated tests to reproduce bugs and guarantee they never regress.

- 
Flakiness Eradication: Treat flaky tests as a critical system anomaly. Track, isolate, and eliminate them to maintain absolute trust in the automation suite.

- 
Actionable ROI: Track and report on key QA operational metrics (Test Coverage, Automation Pass Rates, Execution Time, and Defect Leakage Rate) to optimize delivery speed.

- 
AI-Driven Testing: Pioneer the usage of modern AI tools to accelerate test case generation, optimize test suites, and intelligently predict defect hot-spots.

Qualifications & Profile:

- 
Technical Background: Strong background as a Senior SDET (Software Development Engineer in Test) or QA Automation Lead, with proven experience testing complex enterprise SaaS, distributed systems, big data engines, or data platforms.

- 
Automation Mastery: Deep expertise in coding languages (Java, Python, or Go) and modern testing frameworks (e.g., Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or custom-built frameworks). Exceptional SQL skills and API testing expertise are mandatory.

- 
Extreme Ownership: Exceptional proactive behavior. You do not wait for code to be delivered to think about testing. You anticipate regressions, challenge architectural assumptions, and aggressively push for built-in quality.

- 
CI/CD & Infrastructure Savvy: Hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, cloud platforms (AWS/Azure/GCP), and version control workflows (GitHub). You understand how infrastructure impacts application stability.

- 
AI & Innovation Adaptability: Savvy on using AI assistants and generative AI tools to write smarter test suites, mock data, and analyze test failures efficiently.

- 
Communication: Exceptional verbal and written English communication skills. Ability to stand your ground on quality metrics while maintaining collaborative alignment with engineering leadership.

What We Offer:

- Collaboration with a passionate and diverse team.

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

- Flexible work arrangements (remote or hybrid).
